levels.title: Oral Language & Phonological Foundation
levels.description: Listen, speak, and play with sounds in words. Grade R–1, voice only, entry level. All 8 skills must be shown correctly at least 3 times each, across 2 different sessions at least 24 hours apart, with no help or hints.

atomic_skills.title: Following 2–3 step spoken instructions
atomic_skills.description: Follow spoken instructions with 2–3 steps, in the right order. The learner hears the instruction once and carries out each step correctly — no repeating, no hints.

error_signatures.description: A step was skipped entirely
error_signatures.example: Learner completes steps 1 and 3 but omits step 2

error_signatures.description: Steps completed but done out of order
error_signatures.example: Learner does step 3 before step 1

error_signatures.description: Learner needed the instruction repeated before responding
error_signatures.example: Learner asks 'Can you say that again?' before attempting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OMISSION: rebuild from 1-step instructions. SEQUENCE_ERROR: add visual order cues. PROMPT_DEPENDENCE: shorten instruction length.

atomic_skills.title: Retelling a story in order
atomic_skills.description: Retell a story they heard, with at least 3 events in the correct sequence. The learner uses their own words to describe what happened, in order.

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 events recalled in the retell
error_signatures.example: Learner only mentions one thing that happened in the story

error_signatures.description: Events recalled but placed out of order
error_signatures.example: Learner describes the ending before the beginning

error_signatures.description: Learner cannot recall events from the source story without prompting
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'I don't remember' or gives unrelated content

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LOW_EVENT_COUNT: scaffold with 'What happened next?' prompts. SEQUENCE_INVERSION: model using physical props. COPY_FAIL: model using physical props.

atomic_skills.title: Speaking in full sentences
atomic_skills.description: Speak in full sentences — not just single words or fragments. Every response should have a subject and a verb, without needing prompting.

error_signatures.description: Response is missing a subject or verb
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'Running fast' instead of 'The dog is running fast'

error_signatures.description: Only a single word produced as the full response
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'Dog' when asked to describe the picture

error_signatures.description: Learner repeats the prompt verbatim instead of constructing a response
error_signatures.example: Prompt: 'What did you do today?' Response: 'What did you do today?'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: FRAGMENT: provide sentence frame scaffolds. ONE_WORD: expand and recast. ECHO: switch to open-ended questions only.

atomic_skills.title: Spotting and making rhymes
atomic_skills.description: Identify words that rhyme, and make up their own rhyming words. The learner hears a word and says a word that sounds the same at the end — and can tell when two words rhyme or don't.

error_signatures.description: A non-rhyming word is produced in response to a rhyme prompt
error_signatures.example: Given 'cat', learner says 'dog' instead of 'hat'

error_signatures.description: Learner gives a word linked by meaning rather than sound
error_signatures.example: Given 'cat', learner says 'kitten' (related meaning, not rhyme)

error_signatures.description: Learner incorrectly identifies a non-rhyming pair as a rhyme
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'cat' and 'can' rhyme

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NON_RHYME_GEN: run rhyme discrimination drills first. ASSOCIATION_ERROR: explicitly teach 'sounds like, not means like'.

atomic_skills.title: Clapping out the parts of a word
atomic_skills.description: Clap out the syllables in a spoken word, and blend syllables back together. The learner taps once for each part of a word, and can merge syllable chunks back into the whole word.

error_signatures.description: Too many taps — more syllables counted than exist
error_signatures.example: Learner taps 3 times for 'rain-bow' (2 syllables)

error_signatures.description: Two syllables collapsed into one tap
error_signatures.example: Learner taps once for 'cup-board' (2 syllables)

error_signatures.description: Learner cannot merge the syllable segments back into the full word
error_signatures.example: Given 'rain' + 'bow', learner cannot produce 'rainbow'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OVER_SEG: model with learner's own name. UNDER_SEG: exaggerate each syllable. BLEND_FAIL: reduce to 2-syllable words.

atomic_skills.title: Hearing the first and last sound in a word
atomic_skills.description: Pick out the first and last sound in a word. The learner hears a spoken word and says the very first sound, then the very last sound — with no letters or print involved.

error_signatures.description: Wrong first sound identified
error_signatures.example: For 'sun', learner says /z/ instead of /s/

error_signatures.description: Wrong last sound identified
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner says /k/ instead of /t/

error_signatures.description: Learner says the letter name instead of the phoneme sound
error_signatures.example: For 'bat', learner says 'bee' instead of /b/

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ONSET_ERROR: drill with alliterative word sets. CODA_ERROR: use CVC words with a clapped final tap. NAME_SUB: explicitly teach 'the sound, not the name'.

atomic_skills.title: Breaking words into separate sounds and back
atomic_skills.description: Break a word into its individual sounds, and blend sounds back into a word. The learner says each separate sound in a spoken word one by one, and can put a list of sounds back together into the right word.

error_signatures.description: A phoneme is missing from the segmented output
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner says /k/ /t/ omitting the vowel /a/

error_signatures.description: An extra phoneme inserted into the segmented output
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner says /k/ /a/ /t/ /s/

error_signatures.description: Phonemes produced in wrong order
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner says /t/ /a/ /k/

error_signatures.description: Blended output doesn't match the target word
error_signatures.example: Given /k/ /a/ /t/, learner produces 'cut' instead of 'cat'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PHONEME_OMIT: Elkonin box drill (a box for each sound). SEQ_ERROR: use a left-to-right physical counter. BLEND_FAIL: reduce to 2-phoneme sequences.

atomic_skills.title: Swapping or removing sounds to make new words
atomic_skills.description: Swap or remove a sound in a word to make a new word. For example: say 'bat' without the /b/, or change the /b/ in 'bat' to /s/ to make 'sat'. The learner manipulates sounds in their head — no print involved.

error_signatures.description: Incorrect phoneme was deleted from the word
error_signatures.example: Asked to say 'bat' without /b/, learner says 'ba' removing the final /t/

error_signatures.description: Wrong phoneme was swapped in during substitution task
error_signatures.example: Asked to change /b/ in 'bat' to /s/, learner produces 'tab'

error_signatures.description: Response took longer than 5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner pauses more than 5 seconds before responding

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_PHONEME_REMOVED: segment the word before deleting. HIGH_LATENCY: reduce to onset deletion only and rebuild automaticity.

levels.title: Alphabetic Code Construction
levels.description: Learn the sound each letter makes, quickly and automatically. Grade 1, voice + text. Unlocks after Level 1. At least 95% accuracy with mean response time of 2.5 seconds or less, confirmed across 2 separate sessions. Speed matters as much as accuracy — average response time over 4 seconds sends the learner back to Level 1 drills.

atomic_skills.title: Saying the sound for each letter
atomic_skills.description: Say the sound (not the name) of every letter — uppercase and lowercase — within 2.5 seconds. When shown a letter, the learner says the phoneme it makes, not what it's called.

error_signatures.description: Learner says the letter name instead of the phoneme sound
error_signatures.example: Sees 'b', says 'bee' instead of /b/

error_signatures.description: Incorrect sound produced for the letter shown
error_signatures.example: Sees 's', produces /z/ sound

error_signatures.description: Response time exceeds 2.5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner pauses 3 seconds before producing the sound

error_signatures.description: Learner confuses visually similar letters such as b/d, p/q, or m/w
error_signatures.example: Sees 'b', produces /d/ sound

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NAME_HABIT: run 'sound only' drill mode. HIGH_LATENCY: timed flashcard mode. VISUAL_CONF: dedicated anchor drill before returning to full set.

atomic_skills.title: Matching letters and sounds both ways
atomic_skills.description: Connect letters to sounds in both directions: letter → sound, and sound → letter. The learner can go from a letter to its sound AND pick the right letter when they hear a sound.

error_signatures.description: Passes forward (letter to sound) but fails backward (sound to letter)
error_signatures.example: Can say /b/ for 'b' but cannot select 'b' when hearing /b/

error_signatures.description: Two different letters mapped to the same phoneme
error_signatures.example: Both 'b' and 'd' mapped to the same /b/ sound

error_signatures.description: No discernible letter-to-sound mapping — responses appear random
error_signatures.example: Learner selects random letters when hearing phonemes

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: UNIDIRECTIONAL_ONLY: backward mapping drills. CONFLATION: isolate the confused pair and drill the contrast. RANDOM: regress to L1.

atomic_skills.title: Telling apart look-alike letters (b/d, p/q)
atomic_skills.description: Correctly tell apart look-alike letters: b/d, p/q, and m/w. The learner can look at each letter and say exactly which one it is — no mix-ups allowed.

error_signatures.description: b and d swapped
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'b' as 'd' or vice versa

error_signatures.description: p and q swapped
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'p' as 'q' or vice versa

error_signatures.description: m and w swapped
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'm' as 'w' or vice versa

error_signatures.description: Correct in some orientations but not others
error_signatures.example: Correctly identifies 'b' in isolation but not in flashcard context

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Any pair failure: specific anchor drill for that pair. Do not advance Tier 1 until zero errors on all three pairs.

atomic_skills.title: Reading two-letter sounds like 'sh' and 'ch'
atomic_skills.description: Produce the correct single sound for digraphs like sh, ch, th, wh, ck, and ng. Two letters make one sound — the learner says that one sound, not two separate letter sounds.

error_signatures.description: Learner produces two separate letter sounds instead of one digraph phoneme
error_signatures.example: For 'sh', learner says /s/ then /h/ separately instead of /sh/

error_signatures.description: Incorrect phoneme produced for the digraph
error_signatures.example: For 'ch', learner says /k/ instead of /ch/

error_signatures.description: Response time exceeds 2.5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner takes 3 seconds to retrieve digraph sound

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COMPONENT_PHONEMES: model the digraph as a single unit. WRONG_SOUND: return to individual letter sounds. SLOW: timed drill mode.

atomic_skills.title: Reading letter-pair sounds like 'st' and 'bl'
atomic_skills.description: Say both sounds in a consonant blend (e.g. 'st', 'bl') in the right order. The learner sees a blend and says each of its two sounds correctly, one after the other — no vowel sneaking in between.

error_signatures.description: Second phoneme of the blend produced before the first
error_signatures.example: For 'st', learner produces /t/ /s/ instead of /s/ /t/

error_signatures.description: Only one phoneme of the blend produced
error_signatures.example: For 'st', learner only says /s/

error_signatures.description: A vowel sound inserted between the consonants of the blend
error_signatures.example: For 'st', learner says /s/ /uh/ /t/

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ORDER_REVERSAL: left-to-right physical cue. INTRUSIVE_VOWEL: exaggerate the blend inside a word with no pause; model until eliminated.

atomic_skills.title: Reading vowel pairs like 'ai' and 'ee'
atomic_skills.description: Say the correct sound for vowel teams like ai, ee, oa, and oo — as one sound, not two. The learner sees a vowel team and produces a single fused phoneme, not two separate vowel sounds.

error_signatures.description: Learner produces two individual vowel sounds instead of the team phoneme
error_signatures.example: For 'ai', learner says /a/ then /i/ instead of the long /a/ sound

error_signatures.description: Long vowel of the wrong letter produced
error_signatures.example: For 'oa', learner produces the long /a/ sound instead of long /o/

error_signatures.description: Response time exceeds 2.5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner pauses more than 2.5 seconds before responding

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SPLIT_VOWEL: present vowel team inside a known word first (e.g., 'rain' contains 'ai'). WRONG_LONG_VOWEL: contrast drill between the confused teams.

atomic_skills.title: Saying any letter sound quickly without thinking
atomic_skills.description: Retrieve the correct sound for any letter, digraph, blend, or vowel team from a mixed 40-item set in under 2.5 seconds. Tests whether sound knowledge is fully automatic across all phonogram types — not just one category at a time.

error_signatures.description: Any single item exceeds 4.0 seconds latency
error_signatures.example: Learner takes 5 seconds to retrieve the sound for 'ng'

error_signatures.description: Total accuracy falls below 95%
error_signatures.example: Learner gets 3 or more items wrong in a 40-item set

error_signatures.description: Multiple failures within the same phonogram type (e.g., all digraph errors)
error_signatures.example: Learner fails 'sh', 'ch', and 'th' but passes all single letters

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LATENCY_OUTLIER: target failed items in isolation. CLUSTER_FAIL: drill that phonogram cluster type; return to full set only after cluster passes.

atomic_skills.title: Blending sounds together to make a word
atomic_skills.description: Blend a sequence of individual sounds spoken one at a time into the full word. The learner hears each sound in isolation and combines them smoothly to produce the complete word — the opposite direction to encoding.

error_signatures.description: Only 1-2 phonemes produced instead of the full blended word
error_signatures.example: Given /k/ /ae/ /t/, learner only says /k/ /ae/

error_signatures.description: Correct phonemes blended but in wrong order
error_signatures.example: Given /k/ /ae/ /t/, learner produces 'tack'

error_signatures.description: Output phonemically unrelated to the target word
error_signatures.example: Given /k/ /ae/ /t/, learner produces 'big'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PARTIAL_BLEND: reduce to 2-phoneme blends. TARGET_MISS: return to L1.C2 blending task.

levels.title: Encoding Consolidation — HARD GATE 1
levels.description: Spell words by matching sounds to letters. Grade 2, mainly text input. HARD GATE 1: Level 4 is completely locked until this level is passed — no exceptions, no overrides. At least 80% of encoded words must be plausible (every sound has a letter, in the right order), including made-up words, confirmed across 3 separate sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Spelling short words by sound
atomic_skills.description: Type a plausible spelling for short CVC words (including made-up ones like 'zolp') — one letter per sound. The learner hears a word and types each sound as a letter, in the correct order, without help.

error_signatures.description: Vowel phoneme has no grapheme in the typed output
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner types 'ct'

error_signatures.description: Any phoneme is left unrepresented in the typed output
error_signatures.example: For 'sun', learner types 'sn'

error_signatures.description: Output shares only 1 or fewer phonemes with the target — suggests visual guessing
error_signatures.example: For 'blof', learner types 'blow' — a real word with no phonetic match

error_signatures.description: Phonemes encoded but in wrong left-to-right order
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner types 'tac'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: VOWEL_OMIT: Elkonin box drill with explicit vowel slot. VISUAL_GUESS: nonsense-only words. SEQ_ERROR: left-to-right tap before writing.

atomic_skills.title: Spelling longer words with letter-pairs
atomic_skills.description: Type plausible spellings for longer words with blends and digraphs (e.g. 'stomp', 'chin'). The learner must capture every sound in the word — including blends — in the right order, without dropping letters.

error_signatures.description: One phoneme of a blend omitted in the encoding
error_signatures.example: For 'stop', learner types 'sop' omitting the /t/

error_signatures.description: Blend phonemes encoded in wrong order
error_signatures.example: For 'stop', learner types 'tsop'

error_signatures.description: A digraph encoded as two separate letters rather than as a unit
error_signatures.example: For 'ship', learner types 'shipp' treating sh as two sounds

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: BLEND_PARTIAL: isolate blend in speech, tap each phoneme, then encode one at a time. DIGRAPH_SPLIT: model digraph as a single unit.

atomic_skills.title: Spelling new words by sounding them out
atomic_skills.description: Encode unfamiliar real words using sound logic — not from memory. The learner must break each new word into sounds and find a letter for each one, proving they are using the phonics code rather than remembering what words look like.

error_signatures.description: Output matches a common word without phonetic logic — suggests visual memorisation
error_signatures.example: For an unfamiliar word, learner writes a known high-frequency word that doesn't match phonetically

error_signatures.description: Inconsistent phoneme-grapheme mapping for the same phoneme across different words
error_signatures.example: The /sh/ sound spelled 'sh' in one word but 's' in another with no pattern

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: MEMORISATION_FLAG: switch to nonsense words immediately. PHONEME_GUESSING: return to L2 phonogram drill for the failing phoneme type.

atomic_skills.title: Spelling made-up words by sound
atomic_skills.description: Encode made-up words with plausible phoneme-to-letter matches — this is mandatory for passing Hard Gate 1. Because the word doesn't exist in memory, the only way to spell it correctly is to use the phonics code. This skill proves the learner is a coder, not a memoriser.

error_signatures.description: Learner writes a real word instead of encoding the nonsense word — automatic fail
error_signatures.example: For 'blof', learner writes 'blow'

error_signatures.description: A phoneme from the nonsense word is missing in the encoding
error_signatures.example: For 'spund', learner writes 'spud' omitting /n/

error_signatures.description: A grapheme used that has no phoneme correspondence to the target
error_signatures.example: For 'crait', learner writes 'xqzt' — no phonetic relationship

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REAL_WORD_SUB: explicit instruction 'write what you hear, not a real word'. Return to CVC nonsense words only.

atomic_skills.title: Writing every sound in the right order
atomic_skills.description: Write every sound in a spoken word, in the correct left-to-right order — no sounds missing. The learner must account for every phoneme from the first sound to the last, with nothing skipped and nothing out of order.

error_signatures.description: The same position in words is omitted repeatedly
error_signatures.example: Learner consistently omits the final consonant across multiple words

error_signatures.description: Phonemes swapped in the encoded output
error_signatures.example: For 'was', learner types 'saw'

error_signatures.description: Extra phoneme represented in the encoding
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner types 'catt'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OMISSION_PATTERN: identify the position; drill targeting that slot. TRANSPOSITION: left-to-right sweep cue before encoding.

atomic_skills.title: Catching and fixing spelling mistakes
atomic_skills.description: When a spelling attempt is wrong, go back and fix it using sound reasoning — not guessing. The learner notices that their spelling doesn't match the sounds in the word and makes a targeted correction, not a random one.

error_signatures.description: The change shows no phonetic improvement — revision is random
error_signatures.example: Learner changes 'xqzt' to 'xqzp' — neither has phonetic logic

error_signatures.description: Learner never revises even when output is implausible
error_signatures.example: Learner submits 'xqzt' for 'cat' without any attempt to self-check

error_signatures.description: Revision is more complex but less plausible than the original
error_signatures.example: Learner changes a plausible 'kat' to an implausible 'cqat'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: RANDOM_REVISION: teach the check strategy 'say it slowly, tap each sound, match letters'. NO_SELF_CORRECTION: prompt 'Check: does every sound have a letter?'

levels.title: Decoding & Fluency Construction
levels.description: Read aloud smoothly, in phrases, at a natural pace. Grade 2–3, voice required. Unlocks after Hard Gate 1. Read at 60 or more words per minute, with a prosody (phrasing) score of 70% or above, and a self-correction rate of 50% or above — confirmed across 2 separate sessions by voice.

atomic_skills.title: Reading new words by sounding them out
atomic_skills.description: Read unfamiliar phonetic words aloud, producing each sound correctly. The learner sees a word they haven't memorised and reads it by applying their phonics knowledge — each sound in the right order, nothing skipped.

error_signatures.description: A phoneme replaced by a different phoneme
error_signatures.example: For 'pin', learner reads 'pan'

error_signatures.description: A phoneme absent from the spoken output
error_signatures.example: For 'step', learner reads 'sep'

error_signatures.description: Output phonemically unrelated to target — visual guessing detected
error_signatures.example: For 'drip', learner says 'drop' — visually similar but phonemically wrong

error_signatures.description: Response time exceeds 5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner stares at the word for 6 seconds before attempting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PHONEME_SUB: identify substitution pattern (onset/coda/vowel?) and drill that phonogram. WHOLE_WORD_GUESS: return to L3 encoding.

atomic_skills.title: Sounding out made-up words to prove the code
atomic_skills.description: Read made-up words aloud using the phonics code — not guessing from memory. Because the word has never been seen before, the only way to read it is to decode it sound by sound. Producing a real word instead is an automatic fail.

error_signatures.description: Reads a real word instead of decoding the nonsense word
error_signatures.example: For 'blof', learner reads 'blow'

error_signatures.description: Phoneme accuracy below 70% — output not recognisably related to target
error_signatures.example: For 'spund', learner produces a string that shares no sounds with the target

error_signatures.description: Learner refuses to attempt the nonsense word
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'That's not a real word, I can't read it'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REAL_WORD_SUB: explicit instruction 'read what you see'. REFUSAL: explain the purpose 'we're practising the code, not the word'.

atomic_skills.title: Reading lines in the correct order
atomic_skills.description: Read words in the correct printed order from left to right, without skipping or repeating lines. The learner tracks each line consistently — no jumping ahead, no going back to a previous line, no missing words.

error_signatures.description: Learner reads from the wrong line
error_signatures.example: Learner jumps from line 2 to line 4, skipping line 3

error_signatures.description: Learner reads an earlier word out of sequence
error_signatures.example: Learner re-reads a word from the beginning of the line mid-passage

error_signatures.description: Repeats a word without intending to self-correct
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'the the cat sat' without self-correcting the repeated 'the'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LINE_SKIP: text with explicit line guides; reduce column width. BACKWARD_JUMP: return to single-sentence texts.

atomic_skills.title: Reading words as one whole, not letter by letter
atomic_skills.description: Stop sounding out letter-by-letter — read words as whole units. The learner recognises the full word pattern at once rather than sounding each letter individually. This is the shift from decoding to automatic word recognition.

error_signatures.description: Explicit subvocalised sounding of individual letters detected before the word is produced
error_signatures.example: Learner says /k/... /a/... /t/... then 'cat'

error_signatures.description: First 1-2 letters sounded then word completed
error_signatures.example: Learner says /s/... /t/... then 'stop'

error_signatures.description: More than 3-second pause without any output
error_signatures.example: Learner stares at word for 4+ seconds in silence

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LETTER_BY_LETTER: whole-word pattern flash drills; timed repeated reading. SILENT_STALL: return to single-word decoding.

atomic_skills.title: Reading aloud in natural phrases
atomic_skills.description: Read connected text in phrases of at least 2 words, pausing at punctuation rather than after every single word. Reading sounds natural and grouped — not robotic and word-by-word. Punctuation marks shape the phrasing.

error_signatures.description: Prosody score falls below 60%
error_signatures.example: Learner pauses randomly throughout sentences rather than at punctuation

error_signatures.description: Pause detected after every single word
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'The... cat... sat... on... the... mat'

error_signatures.description: Fluent phrasing present but reading rate below 40 WPM
error_signatures.example: Learner groups words correctly but reads very slowly

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LOW_PROSODY: echo reading — system models a phrase, learner echoes. WORD_BY_WORD: mark phrase boundaries before reading; teach punctuation cues.

atomic_skills.title: Noticing when reading doesn't make sense
atomic_skills.description: Notice when a word doesn't make sense in context, and re-read to fix it. The learner catches their own errors by listening to whether the sentence makes sense — then goes back and reads the problem word correctly.

error_signatures.description: Zero self-corrections despite meaning violations occurring
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'The horse sat on the house' without correcting 'horse' for 'mouse'

error_signatures.description: Re-reads correct segments unnecessarily
error_signatures.example: Learner re-reads correctly decoded words multiple times without error

error_signatures.description: Visually similar but semantically wrong word used and not corrected
error_signatures.example: Reads 'horse' for 'house' — visually similar, semantically wrong

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_MONITOR: post-passage check 'Did everything make sense?'. DECODING_SUB: return to L4.A1 phoneme accuracy drills.

levels.title: Comprehension & Language Expansion
levels.description: Understand what you read and explain your thinking. Grade 3, voice + text. Unlocks after Level 4. Literal comprehension at 80% or above, inferential comprehension at 75% or above, and written response completeness at 80% or above — across 2 separate sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Finding answers in the text
atomic_skills.description: Answer questions about facts stated directly in the text, and point to the words that support their answer. The learner finds the evidence in the passage itself — not from general knowledge or guessing.

error_signatures.description: Answer is factually correct but no text evidence used
error_signatures.example: Learner gives correct answer but uses only their own words with no reference to the text

error_signatures.description: Answer expressed in own words but the meaning has changed
error_signatures.example: Learner paraphrases a sentence but alters the meaning in the process

error_signatures.description: Factually wrong answer given
error_signatures.example: Learner states something that contradicts what the text says

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_TEXT_REF: text-reference habit drill — system highlights the relevant sentence; learner must locate and reference it before answering.

atomic_skills.title: Working out what the text suggests
atomic_skills.description: Draw conclusions that aren't directly stated — and explain the reasoning using words like 'because' or 'this shows that'. The learner reads between the lines and justifies their thinking with evidence from the text.

error_signatures.description: Conclusion not supported by evidence in the text
error_signatures.example: Learner draws a conclusion that contradicts or has no basis in the text

error_signatures.description: Conclusion stated without any linking language
error_signatures.example: Learner states conclusion but omits 'because', 'therefore', or similar connective

error_signatures.description: Restates a fact from the text without drawing any conclusion
error_signatures.example: Instead of inferring, learner just quotes a sentence from the passage

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_CONNECTOR: model inference think-aloud 'This shows ___ because ___ in the text says ___.' Learner attempts with the scaffolded connector.

atomic_skills.title: Retelling what a passage is about
atomic_skills.description: Retell or summarise a passage including the main idea and at least 2 supporting details. The learner captures what the passage was mostly about, plus the key details that back it up — in a logical order.

error_signatures.description: Only details listed with no overarching main point
error_signatures.example: Learner lists three events but never states what the passage was about overall

error_signatures.description: n-gram similarity to source text exceeds 70% — output is a near-copy
error_signatures.example: Learner reproduces sentences verbatim from the passage

error_signatures.description: Disconnected list without logical connectors between ideas
error_signatures.example: Learner lists facts with no 'first', 'then', 'because', or other connectors

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_STRUCTURE: graphic organiser — 3-box structure (Main idea / Detail 1 / Detail 2). Learner fills verbally or in text before writing. Scaffold removed when organiser-independent summaries reach 80%.

atomic_skills.title: Using 'because' and 'therefore' to explain ideas
atomic_skills.description: Use connecting words (because, however, therefore, this means that) to link evidence to conclusions. The learner doesn't just state what they think — they use language that shows the logical connection between the evidence and the point they're making.

error_signatures.description: Conclusion stated with no linking language at all
error_signatures.example: Learner states 'The character was scared. He ran away.' — no connector

error_signatures.description: Connective present but linking the wrong ideas together
error_signatures.example: Learner uses 'because' but connects unrelated clauses incorrectly

error_signatures.description: Connective used but no text evidence provided to support it
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'He was scared because...' but provides no evidence from the text

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CONNECTOR_ABSENT: sentence frame 'I know this because the text says ___.' CONNECTOR_MISUSED: explicit modelling of the logical relationship.

atomic_skills.title: Using new words correctly in sentences
atomic_skills.description: Use newly taught vocabulary words correctly in their own sentences. The learner demonstrates that they understand what a word means by using it in a sentence where it makes sense — not just repeating it back.

error_signatures.description: Word used with semantic plausibility score below 0.4 — meaning is wrong in context
error_signatures.example: Learner uses 'enormous' to describe something very small

error_signatures.description: Learner provides a definition of the word but does not actually use it in a sentence
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'enormous means very big' instead of using it in a sentence

error_signatures.description: Learner uses a different word instead of the target vocabulary word
error_signatures.example: Asked to use 'enormous', learner uses 'big' instead

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: VOCAB_MISUSE: system presents 3 more example sentences. Learner attempts again. Second failure: demote from active vocabulary list; re-present in next session.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a clear, organised answer
atomic_skills.description: Write a structured response with a clear topic sentence, supporting details, complete sentences, and connective language. The learner organises their writing so that the main point comes first, the evidence follows, and the language holds it all together.

error_signatures.description: Complete sentence rate below 60% in a 5-sentence response — fragments throughout
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'Cat. Running fast. No stop.' instead of full sentences

error_signatures.description: n-gram similarity to source text above 70% AND no connector words — copied text with no structure
error_signatures.example: Learner reproduces large portions of the source text with no original organisation

error_signatures.description: Keyword overlap with source text below 1 term in more than 60% of answers
error_signatures.example: Written response makes no reference to anything in the passage

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ERR_FRAGMENTS: reduce to 1-sentence minimum. Oral rehearsal — learner speaks the sentence before writing. Sentence frames active until complete sentence rate reaches 85%.

levels.title: Transition to Academic Reading
levels.description: Read to learn — non-fiction texts, structured data texts, instructions, and proper paragraphs. Grade 4, voice + text. Unlocks after Level 5. Advance (Gate E) when main-idea accuracy ≥60%, paragraph-structure score ≥60%, reading/cloze accuracy ≥70%, and structured-data accuracy ≥60% — across 2 separate sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Finding the main idea of a text
atomic_skills.description: Read a story or information text and state the main idea in one sentence that covers the whole text — not a detail, not a topic label.

error_signatures.description: A specific fact stated instead of the overarching main idea (breadth <40%)
error_signatures.example: For a text about recycling: 'A glass bottle can be melted into a new bottle.'

error_signatures.description: Subject named with no predicate verb
error_signatures.example: Answer is just 'Recycling' or 'the water cycle'

error_signatures.description: A sentence copied word-for-word from the text
error_signatures.example: Learner reproduces an opening sentence verbatim

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: DETAIL_AS_MAIN: 'Write a newspaper headline for this text' — must cover all paragraphs. TOPIC_LABEL: sentence frame 'This text is mainly saying that ___.' VERBATIM_COPY: hide text; restate in own words.

atomic_skills.title: Picking out important details from a text
atomic_skills.description: Identify 2–3 supporting details, each different from the main idea and from each other, and each grounded in the text.

error_signatures.description: Two details say the same thing in different words
error_signatures.example: Both details restate that the dog was lost

error_signatures.description: Detail has no keyword overlap with the source text
error_signatures.example: Learner adds a detail not present in the passage

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: DUPLICATE_DETAILS: 'Each detail must give new information.' INVENTED_DETAIL: learner points to the source sentence before stating the detail.

atomic_skills.title: Retelling a text in order
atomic_skills.description: Retell the content of a text in logical order in their own words, covering beginning/middle/end (story) or steps/sections (information).

error_signatures.description: Units retold out of source sequence
error_signatures.example: Learner describes the ending before the beginning

error_signatures.description: Whole text collapsed into one statement
error_signatures.example: Learner gives a one-line gist instead of an ordered retell

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_ORDER: show text-structure mapping; label sections before retelling. COPY_RETELL: hide the text; learner retells aloud.

atomic_skills.title: Filling in missing words from context
atomic_skills.description: Read a grade-level passage with every 7th word removed and type the correct missing word for each blank (Phase-1 fluency proxy for read-aloud accuracy).

error_signatures.description: More than 3 blank responses in 10 — learner not attempting
error_signatures.example: Learner leaves most blanks empty

error_signatures.description: Plausible meaning but wrong word class
error_signatures.example: Learner supplies a noun where a verb is required

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: HIGH_OMISSION_RATE: reduce passage to 50 words; rebuild confidence. CONSISTENT_WORD_TYPE_ERRORS: targeted word-class drill before returning to passage.

atomic_skills.title: Finding facts in tables and charts
atomic_skills.description: Read a structured data text (text table or data paragraph) and answer a targeted question by locating the correct data point.

error_signatures.description: Answer references an incorrect value or category
error_signatures.example: Learner reports the wrong number from the table

error_signatures.description: Answer taken from surrounding narrative, not the data section
error_signatures.example: Learner answers from the story text instead of the data

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_DATA_POINT: 'Identify the data point the question asks for before answering.' CONTEXT_IGNORE: data-isolation protocol — answer from data only until 60%.

atomic_skills.title: Following written instructions step by step
atomic_skills.description: Follow a step-by-step text and produce the steps in the correct sequence with none left out.

error_signatures.description: One or more steps missing
error_signatures.example: Learner skips step 3 of a 5-step recipe

error_signatures.description: Two steps swapped in order
error_signatures.example: Learner lists step 4 before step 3

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: STEP_OMISSION: number each step explicitly before retelling. STEP_INVERSION: jumbled-order labelling task (e.g. '1=C, 2=A, 3=B') checked against source.

atomic_skills.title: Working out a new word from the sentence around it
atomic_skills.description: Work out the meaning of an unfamiliar word from the surrounding sentence or paragraph.

error_signatures.description: Definition similarity below 0.40
error_signatures.example: Learner gives an unrelated meaning for the target word

error_signatures.description: Learner copies a phrase from surrounding text
error_signatures.example: Learner repeats the next sentence instead of defining the word

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_MEANING: context-clue strategy — 'What do the words around it tell you?' ADJACENT_COPY: 'In your own words, what does it mean?'

atomic_skills.title: Writing a paragraph with a beginning, middle and end
atomic_skills.description: Write a paragraph of 5–8 sentences with a clear opening, supporting sentences, and a closing, in logical order.

error_signatures.description: First sentence does not identify the topic
error_signatures.example: Paragraph starts mid-thought with no topic sentence

error_signatures.description: Adjacent sentence coherence below 0.40
error_signatures.example: Sentences jump between unrelated ideas

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_OPENING: sentence frame 'This paragraph is about ___.' RANDOM_ORDER: sentence-ordering activity before writing.

atomic_skills.title: Linking sentences with 'because', 'so', 'however'
atomic_skills.description: Use connecting words (first, then, because, so, however) correctly to link sentences logically.

error_signatures.description: Cause connective used for a time-order relationship
error_signatures.example: Learner uses 'because' where 'then' is needed

error_signatures.description: Paragraph has no connecting words
error_signatures.example: Sentences listed with no linking language

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_CONNECTIVE_TYPE: connecting-word function chart. CONNECTIVE_ABSENT: require at least 1 connecting word per 2 sentences.

atomic_skills.title: Keeping the same tense throughout writing
atomic_skills.description: Maintain consistent tense (past or present) throughout a paragraph without switching mid-paragraph.

error_signatures.description: One verb in the wrong tense
error_signatures.example: Past-tense paragraph with one present-tense verb

error_signatures.description: Systematically alternates between two tenses
error_signatures.example: Learner switches past/present every other sentence

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TENSE_SHIFT: highlight all verbs; learner checks each against the chosen tense before submitting. TENSE_OSCILLATION: 'Pick one tense at the start and stay in it.'

levels.title: Organised Meaning & Structured Writing
levels.description: Organise meaning and write structured, justified responses. Grade 5, strategic voice + text. Unlocks after Level 6. Advance (Hard Gate 2 / Gate F) when all Level 7 skills meet threshold across 3 sessions, opinion structure is produced without support, and transitions appear unprompted.

atomic_skills.title: Skimming a text for the general idea
atomic_skills.description: Skim a text (headings and first sentence of each paragraph only) and produce a correct general topic statement within the target time.

error_signatures.description: Skim latency exceeds 140 sec — learner read the whole text
error_signatures.example: Learner takes 3 minutes on a skim task

error_signatures.description: Topic coverage below 0.40 across the full text
error_signatures.example: Topic statement covers only the first section

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OVER_READING: timer enforced; system reveals headings and first sentences only. TOPIC_TOO_NARROW: 'What is the whole text about, not just one part?'

atomic_skills.title: Scanning a text for a specific detail
atomic_skills.description: Scan a text for a specific named detail (date, name, statistic) without reading the full text, within the target time.

error_signatures.description: Scan latency exceeds 100 sec
error_signatures.example: Learner reads the whole text to find one date

error_signatures.description: Lists all instances rather than the specific requested detail
error_signatures.example: Learner lists every number in the text

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SLOW_SCAN: 'Look for the key word in the question, then find it on the page.' MULTIPLE_ANSWERS: 'Which one answers the question exactly?'

atomic_skills.title: Working out the writer's purpose
atomic_skills.description: Identify the primary purpose of a text (inform, persuade, entertain) and give one text-based reason.

error_signatures.description: Incorrect purpose classification
error_signatures.example: Learner labels a persuasive advert as 'to entertain'

error_signatures.description: Reason does not reference specific text features
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'because it is interesting'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_PURPOSE: purpose-feature chart; check text against 3 features per type. GENERIC_REASON: require naming a specific language feature.

atomic_skills.title: Using headings, captions and bold to find information
atomic_skills.description: Identify text features (heading, subheading, caption, bold, sidebar) and state the function of each.

error_signatures.description: Identifies a caption as a heading or vice versa
error_signatures.example: Learner calls a sidebar a heading

error_signatures.description: States 'it helps' without specifying what
error_signatures.example: Learner says a heading 'just helps you read'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: FEATURE_MISLABEL: explicit feature glossary with examples. FUNCTION_VAGUE: frame 'The [feature] tells the reader ___ by ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Comparing facts in a table or chart
atomic_skills.description: Read a structured data text with two or more comparable entities and answer a comparison/inference question by extracting 2 data points and producing a comparison statement.

error_signatures.description: Only one data point mentioned
error_signatures.example: Learner states one value without comparing

error_signatures.description: Comparison direction inverted
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'less than' when the data shows more than

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SINGLE_DATA_POINT: require a 'compared to' structure in every answer. DIRECTIONAL_ERROR: highlight both values explicitly before comparison.

atomic_skills.title: Telling fact from opinion
atomic_skills.description: Classify a statement as fact (verifiable) or opinion (personal view) and provide a justification.

error_signatures.description: Personal judgement classified as verifiable
error_signatures.example: 'This is the best book' classified as fact

error_signatures.description: Classification given with no reason
error_signatures.example: Learner labels FACT/OPINION with no 'because'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OPINION_AS_FACT: signal words — should, best, worst, I think. FACT_AS_OPINION: 'Can we check this? Is there a source?'

atomic_skills.title: Writing across more than one paragraph
atomic_skills.description: Write 2–3 connected paragraphs, each beginning with a topic sentence and containing 2 supporting details.

error_signatures.description: Opening sentence does not frame the paragraph
error_signatures.example: Paragraph starts with a detail, not a topic sentence

error_signatures.description: Sentence topically closer to a different paragraph
error_signatures.example: A point about causes appears in the effects paragraph

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_TOPIC_SENTENCE: system supplies the topic sentence; learner writes the rest; support removed over 3 tasks. PARAGRAPH_BLEED: 'This sentence belongs in the other paragraph.'

atomic_skills.title: Starting each paragraph with a clear topic sentence
atomic_skills.description: Use a topic-sentence + supporting-detail structure consistently, with the topic sentence flagging the paragraph's main claim.

error_signatures.description: Topic-sentence breadth below 0.40
error_signatures.example: Topic sentence covers only one detail of the paragraph

error_signatures.description: Details come before the topic sentence
error_signatures.example: Learner lists evidence then states the claim last

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NARROW_TOPIC_SENTENCE: rewrite the topic sentence after writing the paragraph. INVERTED_STRUCTURE: 'Topic sentence is always first.'

atomic_skills.title: Writing an opinion with reasons
atomic_skills.description: Write an opinion paragraph that states a clear position and provides 2 distinct supporting reasons.

error_signatures.description: Only one reason clause present
error_signatures.example: Learner gives a position and just one reason

error_signatures.description: Reason is a circular paraphrase of the opinion
error_signatures.example: 'It is good because it is good.'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OPINION_ABSENT: frame 'I believe ___ because ___ and ___.' REASON_RESTATES_OPINION: 'Your reason must give new information.'

atomic_skills.title: Linking paragraphs with transition words
atomic_skills.description: Use transition words (next, also, however, finally, in addition) between paragraphs to signal logical flow.

error_signatures.description: Second paragraph opens with no transition word
error_signatures.example: New paragraph starts with no connective

error_signatures.description: Contrastive transition used between two agreeing paragraphs
error_signatures.example: 'However' used to link two paragraphs that agree

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TRANSITION_ABSENT: fill-in activity on learner's own paragraphs. WRONG_FUNCTION: transition-function chart with examples.

atomic_skills.title: Giving an opinion out loud with reasons
atomic_skills.description: State an opinion orally and support it with 2 distinct reasons using spoken language (text fallback accepted, logged as TEXT_MODE).

error_signatures.description: States reasons but not the opinion
error_signatures.example: Learner gives reasons without stating a position

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 clauses
error_signatures.example: Learner gives a one-clause answer

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OPINION_ABSENT_ORAL: 'Start with what you think, then say why.' SHORT_RESPONSE: elaboration prompt 'Say more — what else?'

atomic_skills.title: Having a back-and-forth conversation
atomic_skills.description: Participate in a 2-turn spoken exchange, responding to a system-generated follow-up question with relevant new content.

error_signatures.description: Turn 2 meaning similarity to topic below 0.40
error_signatures.example: Follow-up answer drifts to an unrelated subject

error_signatures.description: Turn 2 largely repeats Turn 1
error_signatures.example: Learner restates the first answer with no new content

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OFF_TOPIC_TURN2: system simplifies the follow-up question. SHORT_TURN2: 'Can you give an example?'

atomic_skills.title: Summarising a text out loud
atomic_skills.description: Produce an oral summary of a text in logical order, covering the main idea and 2 supporting details.

error_signatures.description: Jumps to details without a main idea
error_signatures.example: Learner lists facts without saying what the text is about

error_signatures.description: Reproduces source sentences aloud
error_signatures.example: Learner recites the text instead of summarising

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_MAIN_IDEA_ORAL: structure 'This text is mainly about ___, and two things that support that are ___.' VERBATIM_ORAL: hide text before summarising.

levels.title: Early Academic Reasoning
levels.description: Think like a student — cause & effect, summarising, comparing sources, audience/purpose, and academic register. Grade 6, mixed text + voice. LOCKED until Hard Gate 2 (Level 7) is passed. Advance (Gate G) when causal accuracy ≥60%, summaries cover 3 key points, comparison validity ≥60%, and academic register is maintained across 2 sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Spotting causes and effects in a text
atomic_skills.description: Identify a cause-effect relationship in a text and produce a statement naming both the cause and the effect with causal language.

error_signatures.description: Effect identified as cause and vice versa
error_signatures.example: Learner says the flood caused the rain

error_signatures.description: Co-occurring events stated as causal without textual support
error_signatures.example: 'It rained and the team lost, so the rain caused the loss'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CAUSAL_INVERSION: 'The cause happens first and makes the effect happen.' CORRELATION_AS_CAUSE: require textual evidence for the causal claim.

atomic_skills.title: Working out who the text is for and why
atomic_skills.description: Identify the intended audience and purpose of a text and provide text-based evidence for both.

error_signatures.description: Audience correctly identified but no textual feature given
error_signatures.example: Learner names the audience with no evidence

error_signatures.description: Purpose misidentified
error_signatures.example: Learner reads a persuasive text as purely informative

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: AUDIENCE_UNSUPPORTED: require evidence before accepting the classification. FEATURE_GENERIC: 'Which specific words or features tell you that?'

atomic_skills.title: Spotting how a writer tries to persuade you
atomic_skills.description: Identify persuasive language features in a text and state the intended effect of each.

error_signatures.description: Names a feature type not present in the given text
error_signatures.example: Learner claims a statistic where none exists

error_signatures.description: Effect stated without a specific impact
error_signatures.example: 'It makes it better' with no explanation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: FEATURE_NOT_IN_TEXT: highlight the feature in the text before naming it. EFFECT_VAGUE: frame 'This [feature] makes the reader feel/think ___ because ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Summarising a longer text in fewer words
atomic_skills.description: Write a summary of a multi-paragraph text to roughly a third of its length, covering 3 key points without copying or adding content.

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 source points represented (coverage <0.40)
error_signatures.example: Summary captures only one main point

error_signatures.description: Copying score ≥60% per sentence
error_signatures.example: Summary reproduces source sentences

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: KEY_POINT_GAP: guided organiser — identify 3 key points before writing. VERBATIM_SUMMARY: hide source text before writing the summary.

atomic_skills.title: Comparing two texts on the same topic
atomic_skills.description: Compare two texts on the same topic by identifying 2 similarities and 2 differences, each grounded in evidence from both sources.

error_signatures.description: Statement references only one text
error_signatures.example: A 'comparison' that only discusses Text A

error_signatures.description: Similarity framed as difference or vice versa
error_signatures.example: 'Both texts differ in that they both mention bees'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SINGLE_TEXT_ONLY: two-source mapping — 'Both share: [X]', 'Text A only: [Y]', 'Text B only: [Z]' must pass before drafting. FRAMING_ERROR: 'Similarities use both/and; differences use but/however.'

atomic_skills.title: Using two sources together in one answer
atomic_skills.description: Read a main explanatory text and a structured data text on the same topic and produce a response drawing on both, explicitly linked with an integration connector.

error_signatures.description: No data point from the structured data text referenced
error_signatures.example: Answer uses only the explanatory text

error_signatures.description: Both sources referenced but not explicitly linked
error_signatures.example: Two facts stated side by side with no linking phrase

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: MAIN_TEXT_ONLY: 'Your answer must include one piece of information from the main text AND one data point.' NO_INTEGRATION_CONNECTOR: integration phrase starters provided.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a clear explanation of a process
atomic_skills.description: Write a structured explanatory paragraph identifying a cause, explaining a process/mechanism, and stating an outcome, using academic transition phrases.

error_signatures.description: Jumps from cause to outcome with no process explanation
error_signatures.example: 'The sun heats water so it rains' with no intermediate steps

error_signatures.description: Contraction or slang detected
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'it's gonna' in an academic paragraph

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_MECHANISM: frame 'This happens because ___. This leads to ___.' CASUAL_REGISTER: flag the word; require a formal replacement; submission gated until corrected.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a short factual report
atomic_skills.description: Write a basic factual report with a title, at least 2 headed sections, and 2–3 sentences per topically distinct section.

error_signatures.description: Paragraphs written without section headings
error_signatures.example: Report is one block of text with no headings

error_signatures.description: Cross-section similarity ≥0.65
error_signatures.example: Two sections repeat the same content

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_HEADINGS: require a title and 2 headings before content. SECTION_OVERLAP: 'Each section must cover a different part of the topic.'

atomic_skills.title: Using formal linking words like 'however' and 'therefore'
atomic_skills.description: Use academic transition phrases (however, therefore, in contrast, as a result, furthermore) correctly between sentences and ideas. (Error signatures follow spec Section 5; the question bank is authoritative for evaluation.)

error_signatures.description: Academic transition used for the wrong logical relationship
error_signatures.example: 'Therefore' used where contrast is intended

error_signatures.description: Casual connector used instead of an academic transition
error_signatures.example: 'And also' instead of 'furthermore'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TRANSITION_MISUSE: academic-transition function chart. INFORMAL_CONNECTOR: flag and require a formal equivalent.

atomic_skills.title: Writing paragraphs that stay on topic
atomic_skills.description: Maintain cohesion across a paragraph using reference chains and consistent topic focus. (Error signatures follow spec Section 5; the question bank is authoritative for evaluation.)

error_signatures.description: Sentence breaks the paragraph's topic chain
error_signatures.example: An unrelated point inserted mid-paragraph

error_signatures.description: Referent of a pronoun is unclear
error_signatures.example: 'It' could refer to two different nouns

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ABRUPT_TOPIC_SHIFT: 'Every sentence should connect back to the topic sentence.' PRONOUN_AMBIGUITY: name the noun instead of the pronoun.

atomic_skills.title: Explaining a process out loud
atomic_skills.description: Explain a multi-step process orally using sequence markers and academic register (text fallback logged as TEXT_MODE). (Error signatures follow spec Section 5; the question bank is authoritative.)

error_signatures.description: Steps explained without sequence markers
error_signatures.example: Learner lists steps with no 'first/then/finally'

error_signatures.description: Slang or contractions in a spoken academic explanation
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'and then it kinda just works'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_SEQUENCE_MARKER: 'Use first, next, then, finally to order your steps.' CASUAL_REGISTER_ORAL: model the formal phrasing; learner repeats.

atomic_skills.title: Defending an opinion out loud with evidence
atomic_skills.description: Defend an opinion orally with textual evidence and acknowledge a counter-point, in academic register. (Error signatures follow spec Section 5; the question bank is authoritative.)

error_signatures.description: Opinion defended without textual evidence
error_signatures.example: Learner repeats the opinion louder instead of citing the text

error_signatures.description: No acknowledgement of a counter-point
error_signatures.example: Learner ignores the opposing view entirely

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_EVIDENCE_ORAL: 'What in the text supports your view?' CONCESSION_ABSENT: frame 'Some might say ___, but ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Describing the steps of a process out loud
atomic_skills.description: Describe a process aloud in correct sequence with no steps omitted or inverted (text fallback logged as TEXT_MODE). (Error signatures follow spec Section 5; the question bank is authoritative.)

error_signatures.description: One or more steps missing in the spoken sequence
error_signatures.example: Learner skips a stage of the water cycle

error_signatures.description: Two steps spoken out of order
error_signatures.example: Learner says condensation before evaporation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: STEP_OMISSION_ORAL: count the source steps first, then retell. STEP_INVERSION_ORAL: ordered prompt cards before speaking.

levels.title: Analytical Reading Foundations
levels.description: Shift from structured academic reading to analytical reading — identifying and evaluating arguments, assessing evidence quality, detecting perspective and bias, writing CEE analytical paragraphs, and delivering oral analyses. Grade 7, hybrid voice and text. Entry requires Level 8 fully mastered (causal reasoning ≥60%, summary ≤⅓ length, comparison valid ≥60%, academic register maintained, confirmed across 2 sessions). Advance when analytical paragraph (CEE) ≥60%, evidence evaluation ≥60%, synthesis ≥60%, oral analysis ≥60%, academic register maintained across 2 sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Spotting the writer's main argument
atomic_skills.description: Identify the central argument of an expository or persuasive text and state it in one sentence.

error_signatures.description: Specific fact or supporting detail stated instead of the overarching central argument. Argument breadth score <40% (RED zone).
error_signatures.example: Learner states a single supporting statistic instead of the writer's overall position

error_signatures.description: Subject of the text named without a position or claim about that subject.
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'This text is about pollution' with no stance

error_signatures.description: Sentence or phrase copied word-for-word from the text rather than paraphrased as an argument statement.
error_signatures.example: Learner reproduces a sentence verbatim from the source

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: DETAIL_AS_ARGUMENT: 'What is the writer trying to convince you of?' TOPIC_LABEL_L9: sentence frame: 'This text argues that ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Telling a claim apart from the evidence behind it
atomic_skills.description: Distinguish the main claim from supporting evidence in an argument paragraph by writing an explicit statement identifying each.

error_signatures.description: Identified claim does not match the actual position of the paragraph (match <0.40).
error_signatures.example: Learner names a minor detail as the main claim

error_signatures.description: Identified evidence is a paraphrase of the claim rather than a specific supporting detail.
error_signatures.example: Learner restates the position again instead of citing a supporting fact

error_signatures.description: Learner writes the same statement for both claim and evidence.
error_signatures.example: Both the claim and evidence sentences are identical

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CLAIM_MISSED: 'The claim tells you what the writer thinks. Start your answer with: The writer argues that...' EVIDENCE_ECHOES_CLAIM: require the evidence to contain a specific fact, example, or quotation, not a restatement of the position. NO_DISTINCTION: sentence frames provided — 'The main claim is ___ / The evidence for this is ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Spotting what a writer is taking for granted
atomic_skills.description: Identify an implicit assumption in a short argument and state the unstated assumption.

error_signatures.description: Stated assumption does not match the logical gap in the argument. Assumption Match score <0.40 (RED zone).
error_signatures.example: Learner names an assumption unrelated to the argument's gap

error_signatures.description: Learner identifies an explicitly stated premise as the implicit assumption.
error_signatures.example: Learner repeats a premise already written in the argument

error_signatures.description: Learner states the conclusion of the argument instead of identifying what must be assumed.
error_signatures.example: Learner restates the conclusion rather than the hidden assumption

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_ASSUMPTION: fill-the-gap: 'What would have to be true for this argument to work?' STATED_PREMISE: system highlights stated premises; learner identifies what is missing.

atomic_skills.title: Judging whether evidence is strong or weak
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate the quality of evidence by rating each piece as STRONG, WEAK, or IRRELEVANT and giving a reason with a quality criterion.

error_signatures.description: Evidence with no logical connection to the claim rated as strong.
error_signatures.example: Learner rates an off-topic statement as strong evidence

error_signatures.description: A rating is given but the reason contains no identifiable quality criterion.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'it is strong because it sounds good'

error_signatures.description: Rating given with no reason or explanation at all.
error_signatures.example: Learner rates evidence as weak with no reason

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: IRRELEVANT_AS_STRONG: criterion checklist: specific / recent / measurable / relevant / reliable source. NO_CRITERION: sentence frame: 'This evidence is [RATING] because it is [CRITERION].'

atomic_skills.title: Spotting a writer's perspective or bias
atomic_skills.description: Identify the perspective of a text and name at least one specific language feature that reveals that perspective, linked with reasoning.

error_signatures.description: Perspective classification incorrect — text classified as pro/con/neutral when the evidence does not support that classification.
error_signatures.example: Learner labels a clearly persuasive text as neutral

error_signatures.description: A language feature is named but not connected to the identified perspective.
error_signatures.example: Learner names emotive language but does not say what view it reveals

error_signatures.description: Evidence stated as 'it uses descriptive words' or similar — no specific word, phrase, or device cited.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'it uses descriptive words' with no example

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_PERSPECTIVE: perspective feature chart: loaded words / selective facts / emotive language / rhetorical questions. GENERIC_EVIDENCE_L9: 'Which specific words or phrases tell you that?'

atomic_skills.title: Combining two texts into one answer
atomic_skills.description: Synthesize information from two texts on the same topic into a single integrated response using a specific detail from each text and an integration connector.

error_signatures.description: Response references only one of the two texts.
error_signatures.example: Integrated response only uses Text A

error_signatures.description: Both sources are referenced but no integration connector links them.
error_signatures.example: Two facts stated side by side with no linking phrase

error_signatures.description: Two separate summaries written rather than one unified integrated response. Integration Cohesion score <0.40 (RED zone).
error_signatures.example: A summary of Text A followed by a separate summary of Text B

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SINGLE_SOURCE_ONLY: two-source checklist — learner writes 'I used Text A: [detail]. I used Text B: [detail].' before submitting. PARALLEL_SUMMARY: text-based integration frame — one sentence naming a point from Text A AND a point from Text B joined by an integration connector.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a clear claim, evidence and explanation
atomic_skills.description: Write an analytical paragraph using Claim–Evidence–Explanation (CEE) structure with a position claim, specific evidence, and an explanation of significance.

error_signatures.description: Paragraph has no identifiable position statement with a text reference.
error_signatures.example: Paragraph opens with evidence and never states a position

error_signatures.description: No specific text detail is cited as evidence.
error_signatures.example: Claim asserted with no supporting text detail

error_signatures.description: Evidence is stated but no explanation of its significance is given.
error_signatures.example: Evidence quoted but never connected to the claim

error_signatures.description: A sentence is unrelated to the paragraph's central argument. Cohesion score <0.40 (RED zone).
error_signatures.example: An off-topic sentence inserted into the paragraph

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_CLAIM_SENTENCE: CEE frame: 'I argue that [CLAIM]. The text shows [EVIDENCE]. This demonstrates [EXPLANATION].' NO_EXPLANATION_SENTENCE: 'Say why the evidence matters.'

atomic_skills.title: Using cautious language like 'may' and 'often'
atomic_skills.description: Use qualifying and hedging language correctly in academic writing with at least two appropriate hedging expressions and no overuse.

error_signatures.description: No hedging expressions present in the paragraph.
error_signatures.example: Paragraph states every claim as absolute fact

error_signatures.description: A hedging word is used where certainty is required by the argument's logic.
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'water may be wet'

error_signatures.description: ≥5 hedging expressions in one paragraph — argument becomes too tentative to sustain.
error_signatures.example: Every sentence in the paragraph contains 'might' or 'perhaps'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: HEDGE_ABSENT: hedging function chart with 8 example expressions. HEDGE_MISUSE: fill-in: paragraph with blanks where hedging is and is not needed.

atomic_skills.title: Giving a claim–evidence–explanation answer out loud
atomic_skills.description: Deliver an oral analytical response using CEE structure: claim signal, evidence reference, explanation clause, and academic register.

error_signatures.description: Response begins with evidence or explanation — no position statement produced.
error_signatures.example: Learner starts speaking with a fact and never states a position

error_signatures.description: No specific text detail named as evidence.
error_signatures.example: Learner states a position but cites no text detail

error_signatures.description: Evidence stated but its significance not explained.
error_signatures.example: Learner names evidence but does not say what it shows

error_signatures.description: Contraction or informal word detected in spoken response.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'it's kinda obvious'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_CLAIM_ORAL: 'Start with what you think the text is arguing.' CASUAL_REGISTER_ORAL_L9: system flags word; learner restates formally.

atomic_skills.title: Judging an argument out loud
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate an argument orally: identify the claim, rate the evidence as strong or weak, and give a reason containing a quality criterion in at least three clauses.

error_signatures.description: Learner evaluates the argument without first stating what the writer is claiming.
error_signatures.example: Learner rates evidence without naming the claim

error_signatures.description: No strength judgment (strong/weak) given.
error_signatures.example: Learner discusses the argument but never rates the evidence

error_signatures.description: Rating given without any quality criterion in the reason.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'the evidence is weak' with no reason

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 complete clauses produced.
error_signatures.example: Learner gives a one-clause answer

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CLAIM_NOT_IDENTIFIED: 3-step prompt: 'What is the writer claiming? Is the evidence strong? Why?' SHORT_EVALUATION: elaboration prompt: 'Say more — what makes you think that?'

levels.title: Evaluative & Argumentative Control
levels.description: Move from analysing arguments to evaluating their logic and writing controlled argumentative essays — logical fallacies, validity, fact/inference/speculation, counter-arguments, three-source synthesis with citation, and formal oral argument. Grade 8, strategic voice and text. Entry requires Level 9 fully mastered (analytical paragraph (CEE) ≥60%, evidence evaluation ≥60%, synthesis ≥60%, academic register maintained, confirmed across 2 sessions). Advance when essay structure ≥60%, grammar GREEN or AMBER, citation ≥60%, across 3 sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Spotting a flaw in an argument
atomic_skills.description: Identify a logical fallacy in a short argument, name the fallacy type, and explain why the reasoning fails.

error_signatures.description: A fallacy is present in the argument but the learner names the wrong type.
error_signatures.example: Learner labels a straw man as an ad hominem

error_signatures.description: The learner names a fallacy type that is not present in the given argument.
error_signatures.example: Learner claims a false dichotomy where none exists

error_signatures.description: Explanation repeats the fallacy label without identifying the specific reasoning flaw.
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'it is a straw man because it is a straw man'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: FALLACY_MISLABEL: fallacy recognition chart with one worked example per type. FALLACY_NOT_IN_TEXT: evidence-first: highlight the flawed reasoning before naming the type.

atomic_skills.title: Checking whether an argument is logically sound
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate the logical validity of an argument by stating whether the conclusion follows from the premises and giving a specific reason.

error_signatures.description: A valid argument judged invalid, or an invalid argument judged valid.
error_signatures.example: Learner judges a sound deductive argument as invalid

error_signatures.description: Validity judgment given with no reason.
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'INVALID' with no explanation

error_signatures.description: Reason simply restates the validity judgment without identifying what makes it valid or invalid.
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'it is invalid because it is not valid'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_VALIDITY: written premise mapping — learner writes 'Premise 1 says [X]. Premise 2 says [Y]. Together they [do/do not] make the conclusion necessary because [reason].' Three correct written maps required before free evaluation. REASON_CIRCULAR_L10: 'What does the conclusion assume that the premises do not establish?'

atomic_skills.title: Telling apart fact, inference, and guesswork
atomic_skills.description: Distinguish fact, inference, and speculation in a multi-paragraph text by classifying each statement and justifying the classification.

error_signatures.description: An inference is classified as a verifiable fact.
error_signatures.example: Learner marks 'the data suggests growth' as a fact

error_signatures.description: Speculation is classified as a grounded inference.
error_signatures.example: Learner marks 'it might rain tomorrow' as an inference

error_signatures.description: Classification given with no reason provided.
error_signatures.example: Learner labels a statement FACT with no justification

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: INFERENCE_AS_FACT: three-category sort drill with signal-word focus (facts: verified data; inferences: 'suggests', 'indicates'; speculation: 'might', 'possibly'). JUSTIFICATION_ABSENT_L10: sentence frame: 'This is [CATEGORY] because ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Comparing how two writers persuade their reader
atomic_skills.description: Compare the argumentative strategies of two persuasive texts on the same topic, naming at least two strategies per text and stating a similarity and a difference.

error_signatures.description: An argumentative technique is present but the learner does not name its type.
error_signatures.example: Learner describes an emotional appeal without naming it

error_signatures.description: A named strategy type is not present in the cited text.
error_signatures.example: Learner claims Text B uses statistics where it does not

error_signatures.description: Strategies from both texts are described in separate statements without comparative framing.
error_signatures.example: Learner lists Text A strategies, then Text B strategies, with no comparison

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: STRATEGY_UNNAMED: strategy catalogue (emotional appeal / expert citation / statistics / repetition / direct address) + identification drill. NO_COMPARISON_L10: text-based strategy comparison frame — 'Both texts use [shared strategy]. Text A alone uses [unique strategy]. Text B alone uses [unique strategy].'

atomic_skills.title: Spotting and judging a counter-argument
atomic_skills.description: Identify a counter-argument within a persuasive text, explain how the author addresses it, and evaluate the quality of the author's response.

error_signatures.description: Counter-argument present in text but not identified.
error_signatures.example: Learner overlooks an acknowledged opposing view

error_signatures.description: Counter-argument identified but author's response not described.
error_signatures.example: Learner names the counter-argument but not how the author answers it

error_signatures.description: No learner judgment on quality of the author's response.
error_signatures.example: Learner describes the response but offers no assessment of it

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COUNTER_MISSED: counter-argument signal-word focus: however / admittedly / while some argue / opponents might say. NO_EVALUATION_CA: sentence frame: 'The author's response [is/is not] convincing because ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Combining three sources with proper attribution
atomic_skills.description: Synthesize information from three sources into one coherent integrated summary, using a specific detail and citation language for each source.

error_signatures.description: One of the 3 sources not referenced in the synthesis.
error_signatures.example: Synthesis uses only two of the three texts

error_signatures.description: Sources referenced without any attribution phrase.
error_signatures.example: Facts stated without 'according to' or any attribution

error_signatures.description: Three separate summaries written rather than one integrated response. Integration Cohesion <0.40 (RED zone).
error_signatures.example: A summary of each text in turn with no integration

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SOURCE_MISSING_L10: source map — one key point per source confirmed before writing. PARALLEL_SUMMARY_3: integration frame — one sentence referencing all three sources required before drafting.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a multi-paragraph argument essay
atomic_skills.description: Write a multi-paragraph argumentative essay with an introduction containing a thesis, at least two CEE body paragraphs with transitions, and a conclusion that introduces no new argument.

error_signatures.description: Introduction thesis breadth <0.40 — does not cover the scope of the essay.
error_signatures.example: Thesis names only a narrow detail, not the essay's overall position

error_signatures.description: Body paragraph missing claim, evidence, or explanation sentence.
error_signatures.example: A body paragraph asserts a claim with no supporting evidence

error_signatures.description: Essay ends without a conclusion paragraph.
error_signatures.example: Essay stops after the final body paragraph

error_signatures.description: Paragraphs not connected by transition words.
