error_signatures.example: Body paragraphs follow each other with no linking phrases

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WEAK_THESIS: thesis reverse drill — write body paragraphs first, then write the thesis. MISSING_CONCLUSION_L10: essay scaffold template with all five required components marked.

atomic_skills.title: Quoting and crediting evidence in writing
atomic_skills.description: Integrate textual evidence into a paragraph using citation language placed at a grammatically correct position with a specific source keyword.

error_signatures.description: Evidence stated with no citation phrase.
error_signatures.example: A quoted fact appears with no 'according to' or source attribution

error_signatures.description: Body paragraph contains no citation language at all.
error_signatures.example: An entire body paragraph cites no source

error_signatures.description: Citation phrase inserted mid-clause at a grammatically incorrect position.
error_signatures.example: 'The data, according to the text shows, increased' breaks the clause

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: EVIDENCE_DROPPED: citation frame fill-in: 'According to ___, [EVIDENCE], which [EXPLANATION].' CITATION_MISPLACED: system highlights the error position and shows a corrected example.

atomic_skills.title: Acknowledging and refuting an opposing view
atomic_skills.description: Write a counter-argument and rebuttal paragraph that acknowledges an opposing view and refutes it with evidence without contradicting the thesis.

error_signatures.description: No acknowledgement of an opposing view in essay or oral argument.
error_signatures.example: Paragraph argues only one side and never raises an objection

error_signatures.description: Counter-argument acknowledged but not challenged or refuted.
error_signatures.example: Learner states the opposing view then moves on without answering it

error_signatures.description: Rebuttal made without supporting evidence.
error_signatures.example: Learner dismisses the counter-argument with no evidence

error_signatures.description: Rebuttal logically undermines the learner's own thesis.
error_signatures.example: Rebuttal concedes a point that defeats the learner's position

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COUNTER_ABSENT_L10: counter-rebuttal frame: 'Some argue [COUNTER]. However, [REBUTTAL] because [EVIDENCE].' SELF_CONTRADICTING_REBUTTAL: 'Does this rebuttal support your thesis or work against it?'

atomic_skills.title: Keeping writing formal throughout an essay
atomic_skills.description: Maintain academic register throughout an extended piece of writing with zero register violations across the full essay.

error_signatures.description: Contraction or slang detected in a body or conclusion paragraph.
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'it's gonna' in a body paragraph

error_signatures.description: Informal 'I think / I feel' used without academic framing.
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'I feel this is bad' instead of an academic frame

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CASUAL_REGISTER_EXTENDED: immediate flag — system highlights the specific word and requires a formal replacement before the paragraph is accepted. FIRST_PERSON_CASUAL: system provides a list of academic first-person alternatives.

atomic_skills.title: Giving a structured argument out loud
atomic_skills.description: Deliver a structured oral argument containing a claim, evidence, counter-argument, and rebuttal in academic register.

error_signatures.description: Response begins without a stated position.
error_signatures.example: Learner opens with evidence and never states a claim

error_signatures.description: No counter-argument acknowledged in oral argument.
error_signatures.example: Learner argues one side only with no opposing view

error_signatures.description: Counter-argument acknowledged but not challenged.
error_signatures.example: Learner raises an objection but never answers it

error_signatures.description: Contraction or slang detected in oral argument.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'that's kinda wrong'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ORAL_NO_COUNTER: oral argument frame: 'I argue [CLAIM]. Evidence shows [EVIDENCE]. Some argue [COUNTER]. However, [REBUTTAL].' ORAL_NO_REBUTTAL: 'What is the problem with that counter-argument?'

atomic_skills.title: Challenging an argument out loud
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate and challenge an argument orally by identifying a logical weakness and challenging it with relevant evidence in at least three clauses.

error_signatures.description: No logical weakness identified.
error_signatures.example: Learner accepts the argument and finds no weakness

error_signatures.description: Challenge made without supporting evidence.
error_signatures.example: Learner objects but cites nothing to support the objection

error_signatures.description: Challenge does not address the identified weakness.
error_signatures.example: Learner challenges an unrelated point

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 clauses.
error_signatures.example: Learner gives a one-clause challenge

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WEAKNESS_MISSED_L10: logical weakness chart (overclaims / lacks evidence / assumes without proof / commits a fallacy). CHALLENGE_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE: 'What specific evidence contradicts this?'

atomic_skills.title: Answering follow-up questions clearly and consistently
atomic_skills.description: Respond to at least three structured follow-up questions probing a stated position, each response adding new information, referencing evidence, and maintaining academic register.

error_signatures.description: Turn meaning similarity to topic <0.40 (RED zone).
error_signatures.example: A follow-up response drifts onto an unrelated topic

error_signatures.description: Turn repeats a previous turn without adding new information.
error_signatures.example: Learner restates the same point on the next turn

error_signatures.description: Turn 2 or 3 contains no evidence reference.
error_signatures.example: A follow-up response gives an opinion with no text evidence

error_signatures.description: Contraction or informal word in any discussion turn.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'yeah it's whatever'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OFF_TOPIC_L10: system re-asks the probe more specifically: 'Focusing on [specific aspect], what evidence supports your position?' REPETITION_L10: 'You have already made that point. What new information can you add?' NO_EVIDENCE_TURN: 'Which part of the text supports this?'

levels.title: Academic Independence & Synthesis
levels.description: Become an independent academic reader and writer — synthesizing three or more sources, reconciling conflicting information, writing extended analytical essays with self-revision, and delivering formal oral presentations, in preparation for the FET Phase. Grade 9, mixed text and voice; formal citation language required throughout. Entry requires Level 10 fully mastered (essay structure ≥60%, citation accuracy ≥60%, argumentative reasoning ≥60%, academic register maintained, confirmed across 3 sessions). Advance when synthesis ≥60%, citation ≥60%, presentation ≥60%, and academic register maintained across 3 sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Combining three or more sources into one answer
atomic_skills.description: Synthesize information from three or more texts on the same topic into a single integrated response with a specific detail and citation language per source.

error_signatures.description: One of the 3 sources not referenced.
error_signatures.example: Synthesis uses only two of the three texts

error_signatures.description: Sources referenced without attribution phrases.
error_signatures.example: Facts combined with no 'according to' or attribution

error_signatures.description: Three separate summaries rather than one integrated response. Integration Cohesion <0.40 (RED zone).
error_signatures.example: A summary of each source in turn with no integration

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SOURCE_MISSING_L11: source map — one key point per source confirmed before writing. PARALLEL_SUMMARY_L11: integration frame — learner writes one sentence referencing all three sources before drafting the full synthesis.

atomic_skills.title: Making sense of sources that disagree
atomic_skills.description: Identify and reconcile conflicting information across two texts by stating the specific contradiction and at least one plausible reason for the difference.

error_signatures.description: Learner does not identify the specific conflicting claims across the two texts.
error_signatures.example: Learner treats two contradictory texts as agreeing

error_signatures.description: Contradiction identified but no explanation for the difference offered.
error_signatures.example: Learner names the conflict but gives no reason for it

error_signatures.description: Reason given as 'one text is wrong' — does not engage with the substance of the difference.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'Text B is just wrong' with no analysis

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CONTRADICTION_MISSED: contradiction mapping — system highlights the two contradictory sentences side by side; learner identifies the specific point of conflict. REASON_DISMISSIVE: reason framework: 'Why might two sources say different things about the same topic?'

atomic_skills.title: Explaining why a writer made certain choices
atomic_skills.description: Identify at least two structural or rhetorical choices in a text and explain, with a purpose verb, how each serves the author's overall purpose.

error_signatures.description: Named structural or rhetorical choice not present in the given text.
error_signatures.example: Learner claims repetition where the text uses none

error_signatures.description: Effect described without a specific purpose verb.
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'it makes it better' with no purpose verb

error_signatures.description: Choice identified but not linked to the text's overall purpose.
error_signatures.example: Learner names direct address but does not connect it to the author's aim

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CHOICE_NOT_IN_TEXT_L11: evidence-first — highlight the feature in the text before naming it. CHOICE_NOT_LINKED: sentence frame: 'This [choice] serves the author's purpose to [PURPOSE] because ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Writing a research summary that credits each source
atomic_skills.description: Write a research summary of 150–250 words integrating at least three sources, each with an attribution phrase, without copying.

error_signatures.description: A claim is made in the research summary without attribution to any source.
error_signatures.example: A key claim appears with no source named

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 key points from the 3 sources represented.
error_signatures.example: Summary covers only one source's main point

error_signatures.description: Copying score ≥65% per sentence in research summary.
error_signatures.example: Sentences reproduced word-for-word from a source

error_signatures.description: Three sources described in isolation rather than synthesized.
error_signatures.example: Each source summarised separately with no integration

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ATTRIBUTION_ABSENT_L11: citation audit — every claim must be attributed before resubmission. VERBATIM_RESEARCH: system hides sources before writing summary.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a longer analytical essay
atomic_skills.description: Write an extended analytical essay of at least four paragraphs with a thesis introduction, at least two CEE body paragraphs with transitions, and a conclusion that references the thesis without new arguments.

error_signatures.description: Thesis breadth <0.40 — does not cover the scope of the essay.
error_signatures.example: Thesis names one narrow detail instead of the essay's position

error_signatures.description: Body paragraph missing one or more CEE components.
error_signatures.example: A body paragraph states a claim with no explanation

error_signatures.description: Paragraph transitions absent or wrong function.
error_signatures.example: 'Therefore' used between paragraphs where contrast is intended

error_signatures.description: Essay ends without a conclusion paragraph.
error_signatures.example: Essay stops after the last body paragraph

error_signatures.description: Casual register detected in any paragraph.
error_signatures.example: A contraction appears in a body paragraph

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WEAK_THESIS_L11: reverse drill — write body paragraphs first, then write the thesis. REGISTER_COLLAPSE_L11: immediate rejection; learner replaces flagged words before resubmission.

atomic_skills.title: Using formal citation language throughout an essay
atomic_skills.description: Use formal citation language throughout all academic writing tasks, matching each citation phrase to its function and never using a citation phrase without a source.

error_signatures.description: A sourced claim has no attribution phrase.
error_signatures.example: A claim drawn from a source appears with no attribution

error_signatures.description: Citation phrase used does not match the type of source use (introduces/quotes/summarises).
error_signatures.example: A summarising phrase used to introduce a direct quotation

error_signatures.description: Citation phrase used with no identifiable source reference.
error_signatures.example: 'According to the study' with no study identified

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CITATION_ABSENT_L11: citation audit of own writing before submission — every sourced claim must be checked and attributed. CITATION_MISMATCH_L11: citation function chart with examples of each type.

atomic_skills.title: Self-checking an essay against clear criteria
atomic_skills.description: Apply a structured five-point self-evaluation checklist to a completed essay, recording PASS or FAIL per criterion with the specific paragraph and sentence for any failure.

error_signatures.description: Learner fails to flag a paragraph that genuinely fails a criterion.
error_signatures.example: A body paragraph with no evidence is marked PASS

error_signatures.description: Learner flags a passing paragraph as failing a criterion.
error_signatures.example: A well-supported paragraph is marked FAIL

error_signatures.description: FAIL identified without naming a specific paragraph or sentence.
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'a paragraph fails' with no location

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CRITERION_MISSED: system highlights the failing paragraph; learner re-reads and re-applies the criterion — 'Does this paragraph have a piece of evidence after its claim sentence?' FALSE_POSITIVE: system explains why the flagged paragraph passes. SELF_EVAL_VAGUE: 'Write the paragraph number and the first three words of the sentence that causes the failure.'

atomic_skills.title: Revising an essay to strengthen its argument
atomic_skills.description: Revise an argumentative draft to strengthen at least one piece of evidence and improve the transition between two specified paragraphs, measurably improving coherence.

error_signatures.description: Revision changes sentence structure only — evidence not strengthened, logic not improved.
error_signatures.example: Learner reorders words but adds no stronger evidence

error_signatures.description: Revised draft shows no improvement in evidence keyword overlap with source text.
error_signatures.example: The revised evidence is no more specific than the original

error_signatures.description: Coherence score unchanged or lower after revision (RED zone).
error_signatures.example: Paragraph cohesion score is the same after revision

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REVISION_SURFACE_ONLY: focused revision protocol — one evidence task + one transition task per session only. NO_IMPROVEMENT: system highlights two sentences at the paragraph boundary; learner writes one new transition sentence connecting them.

atomic_skills.title: Giving a formal 3–5 minute presentation
atomic_skills.description: Deliver a formal 3–5 minute oral presentation with an introduction previewing at least two points, at least two developed points with evidence, sequence markers, and a conclusion in academic register.

error_signatures.description: Introduction does not preview the main points.
error_signatures.example: Learner starts the first point with no preview of the talk

error_signatures.description: A body point contains no evidence reference.
error_signatures.example: A main point is asserted with no supporting evidence

error_signatures.description: Presentation ends without a conclusion.
error_signatures.example: Presentation stops after the last point with no closing

error_signatures.description: Presentation under 2:30 min or over 6:00 min.
error_signatures.example: Learner finishes the whole presentation in 90 seconds

error_signatures.description: Contraction or slang in any section of the presentation.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'that's gonna' during the talk

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_PREVIEW_INTRO: presentation structure template — four-section outline with required components listed per section. TIMING_FAIL: timed practice protocol with mid-point flag.

atomic_skills.title: Answering questions about a presentation
atomic_skills.description: Respond to at least two audience questions using specific evidence from the presentation, addressing each question directly in at least two clauses in academic register.

error_signatures.description: Response does not address the question that was asked.
error_signatures.example: Learner answers a different question than the one posed

error_signatures.description: Response given without any evidence reference from the presentation.
error_signatures.example: Learner answers with an opinion and no evidence

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 complete clauses in the Q&A response.
error_signatures.example: Learner answers with a single short phrase

error_signatures.description: Contraction or informal word in Q&A response.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'yeah it's fine'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: QUESTION_EVADED: Q&A frame: 'The question asks about [X]. In my presentation I showed [EVIDENCE]. This means [ANSWER].' NO_EVIDENCE_QA: 'Which part of your presentation supports this answer?'

atomic_skills.title: Evaluating a long text out loud
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate an extended text orally by stating the overall argument, assessing at least two pieces of evidence with quality criteria, and giving a reasoned verdict in at least six clauses.

error_signatures.description: Overall argument not stated before evaluation begins.
error_signatures.example: Learner begins assessing evidence without naming the argument

error_signatures.description: Evaluation does not assess any specific piece of evidence.
error_signatures.example: Learner gives a general opinion with no evidence assessed

error_signatures.description: Evaluation ends without a reasoned judgment on the text's persuasiveness.
error_signatures.example: Learner describes the text but gives no final verdict

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 6 clauses.
error_signatures.example: Learner gives a brief three-clause evaluation

error_signatures.description: Contraction or informal word detected.
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'it's kinda weak'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ARGUMENT_MISSED_L11: evaluation frame: 'This text argues [X]. The evidence includes [A] which is [strong/weak] because [REASON]. Overall, I find this [convincing/unconvincing] because [REASON].' NO_VERDICT: 'What is your final judgment on the text?'

levels.title: Academic Transition
levels.description: Move from structured analysis to independently constructing thesis-driven arguments — identifying logical fallacies, analysing tone and bias, embedding quotations, and using active and passive voice strategically. Grade 10, mixed reading + writing + voice. Assessment is single-session, with word count checked at submission (no real-time pacing). Advance when structure score >=60%, thesis clarity >=4/5, CEE >=60% per paragraph, counter-argument quality >=3, register >=60%, grammar AMBER or GREEN, 600-800 words, across 3 non-consecutive sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Telling an argument apart from an explanation
atomic_skills.description: Distinguish argument from explanation by stating whether a passage contains a defended position or a described process, with at least one specific textual marker differentiating the two.

error_signatures.description: Process description called an argument with no stance marker
error_signatures.example: Learner labels a described process as a defended position

error_signatures.description: No textual support given for the classification
error_signatures.example: Learner classifies the passage with no quoted marker

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ARG_EXP_CONFUSION: predefined prompt — 'An argument is a position someone must defend; an explanation is a process no one disputes.' Pattern match task before free classification.

atomic_skills.title: Analysing tone and bias in non-fiction
atomic_skills.description: Analyse tone and bias in non-literary text by identifying at least 3 tone markers with the stated emotional register, naming the bias type from a predefined list, and giving at least 1 language-level citation per claim.

error_signatures.description: 'positive/negative' used without a specific predefined label
error_signatures.example: Learner says the tone is 'negative' instead of 'sardonic'

error_signatures.description: Bias described without using the taxonomy name
error_signatures.example: Learner describes one-sidedness without naming framing_bias

error_signatures.description: Tone or bias claimed without textual evidence
error_signatures.example: Learner names a bias with no word or phrase cited

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TONE_VAGUE: predefined tone card; learner selects register-specific word before free analysis. BIAS_UNLABELLED: bias predefined list with examples required.

atomic_skills.title: Spotting persuasive techniques and their effects
atomic_skills.description: Identify at least 3 persuasive techniques per text from the CAPS P1 predefined list, each with its stated intended effect and a specific textual example.

error_signatures.description: Technique name absent from the text
error_signatures.example: Learner claims a rhetorical question where none exists

error_signatures.description: Technique identified but no impact verb stating its effect
error_signatures.example: Learner names a technique without saying what it does

error_signatures.description: Technique and effect given with no textual grounding
error_signatures.example: Learner states an effect but quotes nothing

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TECHNIQUE_NOT_IN_TEXT: evidence-first sequence — highlight technique before naming; effect verb list required. EFFECT_ABSENT: impact verb list required.

atomic_skills.title: Pulling out the hidden assumptions in an argument
atomic_skills.description: Extract implied assumptions from an argument by stating at least 2 unstated premises required for the argument to hold, with at least 1 textual pointer per assumption and a falsifiability test for each.

error_signatures.description: Assumption phrase found directly in the source text
error_signatures.example: Learner cites an explicitly stated sentence as an assumption

error_signatures.description: Removing it does not affect the conclusion
error_signatures.example: Learner names a premise the argument does not need

error_signatures.description: Assumption identified but no disproof condition stated
error_signatures.example: Learner gives no 'IF __ were false, THEN __' test

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: STATED_AS_IMPLICIT: 'Find a belief the argument needs but never says.' Keyword check before submission. FALSIFIABILITY_ABSENT: 'What would have to be true for this assumption to fail?' Required before acceptance.

atomic_skills.title: Building a five-paragraph argument essay
atomic_skills.description: Construct a 5-paragraph argumentative essay with an introduction (thesis plus 2+ argument preview), 3+ body paragraphs (claim plus proof plus explanation), at least 1 counter-argument paragraph, and a conclusion with no new claims.

error_signatures.description: Topic label given instead of a stance
error_signatures.example: Thesis names a subject without defending a position

error_signatures.description: Paragraph count below 4 or above 6
error_signatures.example: Essay has only 3 paragraphs

error_signatures.description: Body paragraph missing at least 1 CEE component
error_signatures.example: Body paragraph has a claim and explanation but no evidence

error_signatures.description: New name or entity introduced in the conclusion
error_signatures.example: Conclusion raises a fresh argument not in the body

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: THESIS_VAGUE: 'This claim must be defeatable — what is your specific position?' CEE_INCOMPLETE: CEE gate — components completed sequentially before free writing.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a clear thesis and topic sentences
atomic_skills.description: Deploy a claimable thesis (position clarity >=4/5) and open each body paragraph with a topic sentence whose meaning connects to the thesis without restating it.

error_signatures.description: Paragraph opens with evidence rather than a claim
error_signatures.example: Body paragraph starts with a quotation

error_signatures.description: Topic sentence restates the thesis (similarity >=0.80)
error_signatures.example: Topic sentence is a near-copy of the thesis

error_signatures.description: Topic sentence meaning connection to thesis below 0.28 (RED zone)
error_signatures.example: Paragraph heading is unrelated to the thesis

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TOPIC_SENTENCE_ABSENT: retro topic sentence drill — write paragraph body first, then write the topic sentence. DRIFT: 'Your paragraph heading must relate directly to your thesis.' Coherence pre-check before body writing.

atomic_skills.title: Building evidence and explanation into your own sentences
atomic_skills.description: Integrate evidence with explanation by building evidence into the learner's own sentence and following it within 2 sentences with an explanation verb linking the evidence to the argument claim, with an explanation-to-evidence ratio >=1.2.

error_signatures.description: Evidence placed as a standalone sentence with analysis absent
error_signatures.example: A quotation sits on its own line with no follow-up

error_signatures.description: Explanation-to-evidence ratio 1.0-1.2 (warning)
error_signatures.example: Each quote gets only one short comment

error_signatures.description: No explanation verb within 2 sentences post-evidence
error_signatures.example: Evidence is cited then a new point begins

error_signatures.description: Explanation does not connect to the argument claim
error_signatures.example: Comment after the quote is off-topic

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: QUOTE_DUMP: sandwich frame mandatory — 'Introduce -> embed -> explain.' Integration check gates submission. ANALYSIS_ABSENT: 'After your evidence, state what it proves — use reveals/demonstrates/suggests.'

atomic_skills.title: Keeping a fully formal voice in academic writing
atomic_skills.description: Maintain formal register across all P3 writing tasks: no contractions, no slang, no personal anecdotes in argumentative context, and hedging within 15% of evaluative sentences.

error_signatures.description: Apostrophe-contracted form detected
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'don't' in an academic essay

error_signatures.description: Informal lexical item detected
error_signatures.example: Learner uses 'kids' for 'children' in a formal argument

error_signatures.description: First-person anecdote in an argumentative body paragraph
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'when I was younger...' mid-argument

error_signatures.description: Hedge proportion above 20%
error_signatures.example: Most evaluative sentences use 'perhaps' or 'might'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CONTRACTION_USED: submission rejected; replace before resubmission. REGISTER_COLLAPSE: full register check before resubmission. HEDGING_OVERUSE: 'State your position clearly — remove hedges or commit to the claim.'

atomic_skills.title: Using a range of complex sentence structures
atomic_skills.description: Use complex sentence structures accurately so that at least 45% of sentences are complex or compound-complex, with zero sentence fragments and zero run-ons.

error_signatures.description: Complexity ratio below 35% across 2 consecutive tasks
error_signatures.example: Almost all sentences are simple

error_signatures.description: Incomplete sentence detected
error_signatures.example: A sentence with no finite verb

error_signatures.description: Comma splice detected
error_signatures.example: Two independent clauses joined by a comma

error_signatures.description: More than 3 subordinate clauses in a single sentence
error_signatures.example: A sentence with five stacked subordinate clauses

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COMPLEXITY_LOW: complex sentence construction drills — subordinating conjunction list; each paragraph must contain at least 1 complex sentence before submission. RUN_ON: automatic flag with the specific sentence highlighted.

atomic_skills.title: Choosing between active and passive voice on purpose
atomic_skills.description: Apply active and passive voice strategically by identifying the voice of given constructions, stating the communicative effect of each, and using both voices in a single writing task with a stated justification for at least 1 passive use.

error_signatures.description: Passive construction misclassified as active
error_signatures.example: Learner marks 'was written' as active voice

error_signatures.description: 'it sounds formal' given without a specific effect type
error_signatures.example: Learner cannot name agency_emphasis or agent_removal

error_signatures.description: Passive construction in own writing with no stated reason
error_signatures.example: Learner uses passive with no justification noted

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PASSIVE_UNDETECTED: auxiliary verb pattern drill (to be + past participle). PASSIVE_UNJUSTIFIED: 'State why you removed the agent here.'

atomic_skills.title: Controlling commas, semicolons and colons accurately
atomic_skills.description: Control punctuation in extended writing with accurate comma usage in at least 90% of contexts, correct semicolons and colons, and zero comma splices.

error_signatures.description: Two independent clauses joined by a comma without a coordinator
error_signatures.example: 'It rained, the match stopped'

error_signatures.description: Semicolon followed by a non-independent clause
error_signatures.example: Semicolon before a sentence fragment

error_signatures.description: Introductory phrase or non-restrictive clause without a comma
error_signatures.example: No comma after a long introductory phrase

error_signatures.description: Colon not followed by a list, explanation, or quotation
error_signatures.example: Colon placed mid-clause

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COMMA_SPLICE: highlighted; 'Replace the comma with a full stop, semicolon, or coordinating conjunction.' SEMICOLON_ERROR: rule reminder — 'A semicolon joins two complete sentences.'

atomic_skills.title: Judging the strength of an argument with criteria
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate argument strength using at least 3 explicit criteria (evidence quality, logical validity, balance) and produce an overall effectiveness judgement with at least 2 criterion-based reasons.

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 criteria named
error_signatures.example: Learner judges using only relevance

error_signatures.description: Effectiveness stated with no criterion reasoning
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'this is weak' with no basis

error_signatures.description: Argument evaluated without any fallacy check
error_signatures.example: No named fallacy and no 'no fallacy detected' statement

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CRITERIA_COUNT_LOW: evaluation criteria card; minimum 3 must be applied before judgement. FALLACY_CHECK_ABSENT: 'Does this argument commit any logical fallacy? Check the predefined list.'

atomic_skills.title: Naming and explaining logical fallacies
atomic_skills.description: Identify logical fallacies by naming the fallacy type from a predefined list, quoting or paraphrasing the fallacious reasoning, and stating why it weakens the argument.

error_signatures.description: Wrong predefined label applied to the reasoning pattern
error_signatures.example: Learner labels a straw man as ad hominem

error_signatures.description: Fallacy named with no text quotation
error_signatures.example: Learner names slippery_slope but quotes nothing

error_signatures.description: Fallacy identified without the effect on the argument stated
error_signatures.example: Learner names the fallacy but not how it harms the argument

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: FALLACY_MISLABELLED: fallacy predefined list with defining characteristics and examples; match description to name before free identification. FALLACY_NO_EVIDENCE: evidence-first — highlight before naming.

atomic_skills.title: Reading imagery and symbolism in literature
atomic_skills.description: Analyse imagery and symbolism in literature by identifying at least 3 images or symbols, stating the literal referent and symbolic meaning, and connecting each to theme or authorial purpose.

error_signatures.description: Referent identified, no symbolic meaning extracted
error_signatures.example: Learner says a dove is a bird and stops there

error_signatures.description: Symbolic meaning with no textual anchor
error_signatures.example: Learner asserts a symbol with no quote

error_signatures.description: Symbol interpreted but not connected to broader theme or purpose
error_signatures.example: Symbol explained but no theme named

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LITERAL_ONLY: four-part frame — 'This image literally represents ___. Symbolically it suggests ___, which connects to the theme of ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Comparing two texts on shared themes
atomic_skills.description: Compare two texts thematically by identifying at least 1 shared theme and at least 1 diverging theme treatment, both grounded in textual evidence from each source, using comparative framing language throughout.

error_signatures.description: Comparison statement cites one source only
error_signatures.example: A 'comparison' that only discusses Text A

error_signatures.description: Theme stated without textual support
error_signatures.example: Learner names a shared theme with no evidence

error_signatures.description: Convergence framed as contrast or vice versa
error_signatures.example: 'Both texts differ in that they both explore loss'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SINGLE_TEXT_REFERENCE: text-based two-source mapping task — learner writes 'Both texts share: [X]', 'Text A only: [Y]', 'Text B only: [Z]' and all three must pass before drafting. FRAMING_ERROR: 'Both: use and/also. Contrast: use however/whereas.'

atomic_skills.title: Writing a balanced discursive essay
atomic_skills.description: Write a discursive essay presenting both sides of an issue fairly (2+ arguments per side), with balanced argument density, formal register, and a clearly stated concluding position with a reason.

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 arguments per side
error_signatures.example: Essay argues only the 'for' position

error_signatures.description: Informal register in a discursive context
error_signatures.example: Slang appears in a discursive essay

error_signatures.description: Essay ends without a stated position
error_signatures.example: Essay stops after presenting both sides

error_signatures.description: Pro minus contra argument count exceeds 2
error_signatures.example: Four pro arguments, one contra argument

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ONE_SIDED_DISCURSIVE: 'A discursive essay explores both perspectives equally — what would the other side argue?' CONCLUSION_ABSENT: 'End with: On balance, I believe ___ because ___.'

atomic_skills.title: Linking paragraphs with the right transitions
atomic_skills.description: Maintain cohesion using transitions so each body paragraph has at least 1 transition whose type matches the discourse function, with no transition repeated more than twice in the essay.

error_signatures.description: Body paragraph with no transition marker
error_signatures.example: Paragraph begins with no connective

error_signatures.description: Contrastive transition in a non-contrastive context
error_signatures.example: 'However' used where addition is intended

error_signatures.description: Same transition used more than twice in the essay
error_signatures.example: 'However' opens four paragraphs

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TRANSITION_ABSENT: transition bank provided; one must be selected before paragraph writing. FUNCTION_MISMATCH: 'Does the relationship here add, contrast, or cause? Select matching transition.'

atomic_skills.title: Embedding quotations smoothly in writing
atomic_skills.description: Embed quotations correctly so at least 90% are built into the learner's own clause with an attribution phrase, correct punctuation, and an explanation within 2 sentences.

error_signatures.description: Quote not embedded in the learner's clause
error_signatures.example: Quotation placed on its own line

error_signatures.description: Quote with no signal phrase
error_signatures.example: Quotation appears with no 'X argues'

error_signatures.description: Comma, colon, or period misplaced around the quote
error_signatures.example: Comma placed outside the quotation incorrectly

error_signatures.description: Quote left unanalysed
error_signatures.example: Quotation cited then a new point begins

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: QUOTE_STANDALONE: sandwich drill — 'X argues that [quote] (attribution + embedding + demonstrates ___).' Full sequence required before submission. ATTRIBUTION_ABSENT: sequence required before submission.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a literary essay with a clear thesis
atomic_skills.description: Write a literary essay with a thesis-driven argument that positions a critical claim (not plot summary), with 3+ body paragraphs of claim plus integrated quote plus analysis, naming a literary technique in at least 75% of analytical points.

error_signatures.description: Thesis describes events with no critical claim
error_signatures.example: Thesis retells what happens in the story

error_signatures.description: Analysis present but no literary technique named
error_signatures.example: Learner comments on effect without naming a device

error_signatures.description: Technique named but no effect stated
error_signatures.example: Learner names 'metaphor' with no effect

error_signatures.description: Embedded quote with no analysis
error_signatures.example: Quotation embedded but not explained

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PLOT_SUMMARY_ESSAY: 'What does the text argue or reveal — not what happens?' Critical claim drill before essay planning. TECHNIQUE_UNNAMED: technique predefined list provided; minimum 1 named per body paragraph.

atomic_skills.title: Synthesising multiple sources in one argument
atomic_skills.description: Synthesise at least 2 sources into integrated paragraphs where both sources are cited in a single paragraph with a comparative or argumentative frame, balanced source distribution, and scaffold frame patterns below 10% of sentences.

error_signatures.description: Sources placed in separate paragraphs
error_signatures.example: Source A in paragraph 1, Source B in paragraph 2, no integration

error_signatures.description: Both sources cited but no framing
error_signatures.example: Two facts stated side by side with no linking phrase

error_signatures.description: Scaffold frame patterns above 20%
error_signatures.example: Most sentences use a provided synthesis template

error_signatures.description: One source above 75% of citations
error_signatures.example: Source A cited eight times, Source B once

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SOURCE_LISTING: integration sentence frame until independent; scaffold removed after 3 passing attempts. SCAFFOLD_DEPENDENCY: frame pattern detection active.

atomic_skills.title: Reading literature in its social and political context
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate socio-political context in literature by identifying at least 1 contextual factor, connecting it to a specific textual element, and stating how the context alters or deepens meaning.

error_signatures.description: Context stated without a predefined taxonomy label
error_signatures.example: Learner mentions 'the time period' without naming historical context

error_signatures.description: Context stated without a textual anchor
error_signatures.example: Context discussed with no scene cited

error_signatures.description: Context and text linked but interpretive effect not stated
error_signatures.example: Context tied to a scene with no 'so what'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CONTEXT_TYPE_ABSENT: context predefined list; label required before linking. SIGNIFICANCE_ABSENT: 'How does knowing this context change how we read the text? Use reveals/complicates/subverts.'

atomic_skills.title: Writing a 600–800 word essay on an unseen topic
atomic_skills.description: Write a 600-800 word coherent academic essay on an unseen topic, meeting the word count, maintaining the 5-paragraph structure, sustaining argument coherence from thesis to conclusion, with zero scaffold dependency. Word count is checked at submission, single session, no real-time pacing.

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 450 words
error_signatures.example: Essay submitted at 380 words

error_signatures.description: More than 900 words (focus concern)
error_signatures.example: Essay runs to 1100 words

error_signatures.description: Missing introduction or conclusion
error_signatures.example: Essay has body paragraphs but no conclusion

error_signatures.description: Body paragraph topic meaning connection below 0.28 to the thesis
error_signatures.example: A body paragraph does not support the thesis

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: UNDER_LENGTH: content sufficiency audit — identify which paragraph is underweight; targeted expansion task. COHERENCE_LOW: 'Your paragraph must directly argue or support your thesis — what does it prove?'

atomic_skills.title: Showing stylistic range across an essay
atomic_skills.description: Demonstrate stylistic maturity through sentence variety across paragraphs, at least 2 distinct rhetorical techniques per essay, and lexical precision with an empty-intensifier rate of zero.

error_signatures.description: 3 or more consecutive same-structure openings
error_signatures.example: Several sentences in a row begin 'The author...'

error_signatures.description: No rhetorical technique in the full essay
error_signatures.example: No anaphora, tricolon, antithesis, or parallelism

error_signatures.description: More than 3 empty intensifiers without evidence support
error_signatures.example: 'very', 'really', 'extremely' used without backing

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SENTENCE_MONOTONY: sentence structure variation drill; each paragraph must demonstrate at least 2 different opening structures. TECHNIQUE_ABSENT: rhetorical technique list; 1 must be inserted and marked before submission.

atomic_skills.title: Finding the main idea and author's purpose
atomic_skills.description: Identify the main idea and author's purpose in an unseen non-fiction text by stating the central claim in one sentence and naming the primary purpose from a predefined list with at least 1 textual marker per claim.

error_signatures.description: Central claim is a topic label rather than a specific position or finding
error_signatures.example: 'This text is about pollution' with no claim

error_signatures.description: Purpose described but not named from the predefined list
error_signatures.example: Learner describes the aim without naming 'persuade'

error_signatures.description: Main idea or purpose claimed without textual support
error_signatures.example: Purpose stated with no phrase cited

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: MAIN_IDEA_VAGUE: 'This text is about X' is a topic label — state what the author claims about X. Sentence-starter scaffold required before free response. PURPOSE_UNLABELLED: purpose predefined list with defining features displayed; learner selects before free identification.

atomic_skills.title: Making inferences from an unseen text
atomic_skills.description: Make inferences from an unseen text by identifying at least 2 implied ideas, providing at least 1 specific textual clue per inference, and explaining the reasoning chain connecting clue to inferred meaning.

error_signatures.description: Inferred idea phrase found directly in the source text
error_signatures.example: Learner cites an explicit sentence as an inference

error_signatures.description: Inference made with no textual anchor
error_signatures.example: Learner infers a point with no quote

error_signatures.description: Clue identified but no chain connecting it to the inferred meaning
error_signatures.example: Clue and inference given with no 'because'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: STATED_AS_INFERRED: 'Find an idea the text hints at but never says.' Keyword check before submission. REASONING_ABSENT: inference chain frame — 'The text says [clue], which suggests [inference] because [reasoning].' Required before acceptance.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a structured summary of a non-fiction text
atomic_skills.description: Write a structured summary of a non-fiction text restating the main idea, including at least 3 key supporting points in logical order, in the learner's own words, within 80-120 words.

error_signatures.description: N-gram overlap with source at or above 35% in any 20-word window
error_signatures.example: Summary reproduces source sentences

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 key points included
error_signatures.example: Summary captures only one supporting point

error_signatures.description: Summary under 60 or over 150 words
error_signatures.example: Summary submitted at 200 words

error_signatures.description: Summary contains only detail without the central argument
error_signatures.example: Summary lists facts but misses the main point

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COPY_PASTE: 'Your summary must use your own words.' Source text removed from view; learner rewrites from memory or notes. SUPPORTING_POINT_COUNT_LOW: structured frame — main idea + point 1 + point 2 + point 3; each slot must be completed before free summary.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a formal letter
atomic_skills.description: Write a formal letter with correct layout, formal register throughout, a clearly stated purpose in the opening paragraph, and a specific request or action in the closing paragraph (180-250 words).

error_signatures.description: Salutation or closing missing or incorrectly formatted
error_signatures.example: Letter has no 'Yours faithfully' closing

error_signatures.description: Informal markers detected in a formal letter context
error_signatures.example: 'gonna' appears in the letter body

error_signatures.description: Opening paragraph contains no purpose statement
error_signatures.example: Letter opens with no stated reason for writing

error_signatures.description: No specific request or proposed action in the final paragraph
error_signatures.example: Letter ends without a call to action

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LAYOUT_INCOMPLETE: formal letter template displayed; each structural element must be labelled before free writing. REGISTER_INFORMAL_LETTER: flagged tokens highlighted; learner replaces each before resubmission.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a persuasive speech
atomic_skills.description: Write a persuasive speech for a specific audience opening with direct address, presenting 2+ supported arguments, including at least 1 rhetorical technique, and closing with a call to action (200-280 words).

error_signatures.description: No audience address in the opening
error_signatures.example: Speech opens with no 'friends' or 'fellow learners'

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 supported arguments
error_signatures.example: Speech makes only one supported point

error_signatures.description: Rhetorical technique claimed but pattern not detectable
error_signatures.example: Learner claims anaphora but no repetition present

error_signatures.description: Speech ends without a directive or desired outcome
error_signatures.example: Speech stops with no closing appeal

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TECHNIQUE_NOT_IN_SPEECH: rhetorical technique list with examples; learner selects and inserts one before submission. CALL_TO_ACTION_ABSENT: 'What do you want your audience to do or believe after hearing this?' Imperative sentence required in closing.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a newspaper article
atomic_skills.description: Write a newspaper article with a headline, a lead paragraph covering at least 3 of the 5 W elements, a body of 2+ supporting paragraphs, factual register, and at least 1 attributed quotation (220-300 words).

error_signatures.description: No short standalone title line detected
error_signatures.example: Article begins straight into prose

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 of 5 W elements present in the opening paragraph
error_signatures.example: Lead omits who, when, and where

error_signatures.description: First-person opinion marker detected in news context
error_signatures.example: 'I think this is wrong' in the article body

error_signatures.description: Quotation used with no attribution phrase
error_signatures.example: A quote appears with no 'according to'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LEAD_INCOMPLETE: 5W checklist displayed; learner completes each slot before body writing. REGISTER_OPINION_IN_NEWS: flagged sentences highlighted; learner rewrites as attributed facts.

atomic_skills.title: Fixing subject–verb and tense errors
atomic_skills.description: Identify and correct subject-verb agreement and tense consistency errors in a provided paragraph, providing the correction and stating the grammatical rule applied for each.

error_signatures.description: SVA violation not identified
error_signatures.example: Learner overlooks 'the team are' error

error_signatures.description: Non-deliberate tense shift not flagged
error_signatures.example: Learner does not catch a present-to-past shift

error_signatures.description: Identified error corrected incorrectly
error_signatures.example: Learner replaces one wrong verb form with another

error_signatures.description: Correction made but rule not stated
error_signatures.example: Learner fixes the error with no rule named

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SVA_MISSED: SVA rule card; learner applies each rule to a targeted sentence set before the full paragraph task. CORRECTION_WRONG: error highlighted; learner shown rule; correction reattempted before proceeding.

atomic_skills.title: Switching between formal and informal writing
atomic_skills.description: Distinguish and apply formal and informal register by identifying at least 3 informal features in a provided text, naming each feature type, and rewriting the full text in formal academic register.

error_signatures.description: Informal feature identified but type not named from taxonomy
error_signatures.example: Learner flags a word but does not call it slang

error_signatures.description: Informal markers remain in the rewritten text
error_signatures.example: Contractions survive in the rewrite

error_signatures.description: Rewritten text meaning similarity to source below 0.45
error_signatures.example: Rewrite changes the original idea

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REWRITE_STILL_INFORMAL: flagged tokens highlighted in the rewritten text; each replaced before resubmission. MEANING_LOST: 'Your rewrite has changed the meaning. Check each sentence matches the original idea.' Sentence-by-sentence comparison required.

atomic_skills.title: Editing punctuation in a paragraph
atomic_skills.description: Edit a provided paragraph for punctuation accuracy by identifying and correcting all comma, semicolon, colon, and apostrophe errors and stating the rule for each correction.

error_signatures.description: Comma splice not identified
error_signatures.example: Learner overlooks two clauses joined by a comma

error_signatures.description: Possessive or contraction apostrophe error not flagged
error_signatures.example: Learner misses 'its' vs 'it's' error

error_signatures.description: Identified error corrected incorrectly
error_signatures.example: Learner replaces a comma splice with another splice

error_signatures.description: Correction made but punctuation rule not stated
error_signatures.example: Learner fixes the error with no rule named

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COMMA_SPLICE_MISSED: comma splice explanation with rule; targeted 5-sentence drill before the full paragraph. APOSTROPHE_ERROR_MISSED: apostrophe rule card (possessive vs contraction); targeted drill before the full paragraph.

atomic_skills.title: Giving a structured short speech
atomic_skills.description: Prepare and present a structured short speech stating a clear position in the opening sentence, providing 2+ supporting points with reasoning, using formal register, and concluding with a restatement of position (100-150 words).

error_signatures.description: Opening contains no stance verb or claimable position
error_signatures.example: Speech opens with a fact, not a position

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 points with reasoning
error_signatures.example: Speech gives one point with no reason

error_signatures.description: Informal markers detected
error_signatures.example: Slang used in the spoken response

error_signatures.description: No concluding position restatement
error_signatures.example: Speech ends without returning to the position

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: POSITION_ABSENT: 'State your view in one sentence. Use: I argue/I believe/In my view.' Stance verb required in the position sentence. SUPPORT_COUNT_LOW: two-point frame — Point 1 [claim + because reason] / Point 2 [claim + because reason]; both slots must be completed.

atomic_skills.title: Answering comprehension questions in full sentences
atomic_skills.description: Respond to a comprehension question about a provided text in full coherent sentences, answering the specific question asked, including at least 1 textual reference, and maintaining formal register (40-80 words).

error_signatures.description: Answer meaning connection to question below 0.30
error_signatures.example: Answer addresses a different question

error_signatures.description: Answer begins with a sentence fragment
error_signatures.example: Response opens with no subject and verb

error_signatures.description: No textual support in the response
error_signatures.example: Answer cites nothing from the text

error_signatures.description: Informal markers detected
error_signatures.example: 'kinda' appears in the answer

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OFF_TOPIC: question reread; 'Your answer must directly address what the question asks.' Sentence starter: 'The text shows/states/suggests...' FRAGMENT_RESPONSE: 'Write at least one complete sentence with a subject and a verb.' Example response displayed.

atomic_skills.title: Summarising what was said in a spoken extract
atomic_skills.description: Summarise the content of a spoken extract provided as a transcript by identifying the main topic, stating at least 2 key points, and noting the speaker's apparent purpose or attitude in the learner's own words (60-100 words).

error_signatures.description: No central topic statement
error_signatures.example: Summary lists points but never states the topic

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 key speaker points included
error_signatures.example: Summary captures only one point

error_signatures.description: No speaker purpose or attitude identified
error_signatures.example: Summary omits why the speaker is speaking

error_signatures.description: N-gram overlap with transcript at or above 35%
error_signatures.example: Summary reproduces transcript wording

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: KEY_POINT_COUNT_LOW: structured frame — main topic + key point 1 + key point 2; each slot must be completed. PURPOSE_ATTITUDE_ABSENT: 'Why is the speaker saying this? What do they want the listener to think or feel?' Purpose verb list provided.

levels.title: Pre-Exam Maturity
levels.description: Deepen analytical control — theme beyond literal interpretation, psychological character analysis, structural text comparison, and 800-word essays building toward NSC exam performance. Grade 11, mixed reading + writing + voice. Assessment is single-session, with word count checked at submission (no real-time pacing). Advance when depth score >=4/5, structural comparison present, counter-argument quality >=4, grammar AMBER or GREEN, coherence ratio >=0.85, 750-900 words, across 3 non-consecutive sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Reading themes beyond the literal level
atomic_skills.description: Interpret theme beyond the literal level by producing a theme statement with a universal abstract claim, naming at least 1 authorial technique used to develop it, and stating an interpretive implication about human experience.

error_signatures.description: Theme word only, no implication
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'the theme is love' with nothing more

error_signatures.description: Valid theme but no authorial technique named
error_signatures.example: Theme stated with no device linked

error_signatures.description: Technique named but no 'so what?' for human experience
error_signatures.example: Theme and technique given with no broader meaning

error_signatures.description: Concrete event stated as the theme
error_signatures.example: 'The theme is that a man dies' instead of mortality

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: THEME_SHALLOW: 'What does this text suggest about people more broadly?' Push to interpretive implication. IMPLICATION_ABSENT: 'What does this theme mean for us as readers — beyond this specific text?'

atomic_skills.title: Analysing what drives a character
atomic_skills.description: Analyse character motivation psychologically by stating the dominant desire, fear, or belief driving behaviour from a predefined list, the textual evidence, and the narrative function the motivation serves.

error_signatures.description: Behaviour described without underlying psychology
error_signatures.example: Learner says the character 'is angry' with no deeper drive

error_signatures.description: Motivation stated without a textual anchor
error_signatures.example: Motivation asserted with no scene cited

error_signatures.description: Motivation explained without a narrative function
error_signatures.example: Drive named but its role in the story omitted

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: MOTIVATION_SURFACE: 'Why does the character behave this way? What do they want or fear most?' Psychological motivation prompt before free analysis. FUNCTION_ABSENT: 'How does this motivation move the story or develop the theme?'

atomic_skills.title: Reading narrative perspective and its effect
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate narrative perspective by identifying the perspective type, stating the effect on reader trust and empathy, and identifying at least 1 specific technique the perspective uses.

error_signatures.description: Wrong perspective type identified
error_signatures.example: Limited third read as omniscient

error_signatures.description: Perspective identified but reader effect not stated
error_signatures.example: Perspective named with no trust or empathy effect

error_signatures.description: Perspective and effect given but no technique named
error_signatures.example: No mention of free indirect discourse or dramatic irony

error_signatures.description: Technique claimed without textual grounding
error_signatures.example: Technique named with no phrase cited

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PERSPECTIVE_MISLABELLED: perspective predefined list with defining characteristics. EFFECT_ABSENT: 'How does this perspective make you trust or distrust the narrator? How does it affect your sympathy?'

atomic_skills.title: Analysing the effect of figurative language
atomic_skills.description: Analyse figurative language impact by identifying the device, stating the literal meaning, the figurative meaning, the tonal effect, and the connection to a structural or thematic pattern in the broader text.

error_signatures.description: No figurative extension given
error_signatures.example: Learner explains only the literal sense of an image

error_signatures.description: Literal and figurative stated but tonal effect absent
error_signatures.example: Meaning given with no tone identified

error_signatures.description: Device analysed in isolation, no connection to the broader text
error_signatures.example: Image discussed with no link to theme or recurrence

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TONE_ABSENT: tone predefined list provided. PATTERN_ABSENT: 'Does this image appear elsewhere in the text? How does repetition or contrast deepen meaning?'

atomic_skills.title: Weaving context into a literary essay
atomic_skills.description: Integrate contextual references in essays by providing a textual anchor and interpretive significance for each reference, built into analytical sentences rather than a separate background paragraph.

error_signatures.description: Context paragraph separated from analysis
error_signatures.example: A standalone historical-background paragraph

error_signatures.description: Context stated without a textual link
error_signatures.example: Historical fact stated with no scene cited

error_signatures.description: Context and anchor given but no interpretive deepening
error_signatures.example: Context tied to text with no 'so what'

error_signatures.description: Context type not from the predefined list
error_signatures.example: Context mentioned without naming it political or cultural

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CONTEXT_ISOLATED: 'Integrate the context into your analysis — don't separate it.' Integration drill: context reference must be embedded in an analytical sentence before submission accepted.

atomic_skills.title: Comparing poems by their structure
atomic_skills.description: Compare poems structurally by stating at least 2 structural features per poem, the effect on pace, tone, or meaning, and the comparative difference or similarity between poems.

error_signatures.description: Compares what poems are about, not how structure creates meaning
error_signatures.example: Comparison discusses subject matter only

error_signatures.description: Wrong structural term used
error_signatures.example: Enjambment called caesura

error_signatures.description: Feature identified but no effect on meaning stated
error_signatures.example: Stanza form named with no effect

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CONTENT_ONLY_COMPARISON: 'Focus on form: stanza breaks, line length, rhythm — how do these create meaning?' Structural analysis framework provided. EFFECT_ABSENT: 'Why did the poet break the line here? What does that pause create?'

atomic_skills.title: Comparing drama and novels on shared themes
atomic_skills.description: Compare drama and novels thematically by identifying at least 1 shared theme and at least 1 diverging treatment, with textual evidence from both forms, and analysing how the medium shapes thematic expression.

error_signatures.description: Compares drama and prose as equivalent forms
error_signatures.example: No mention of stage vs narration differences

error_signatures.description: Comparison statement cites one text
error_signatures.example: A comparison that discusses only the play

error_signatures.description: Theme stated without textual evidence from both
error_signatures.example: Shared theme asserted with evidence from one text only

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: MEDIUM_IGNORED: 'Dramas show; novels tell. How does each form shape how the theme is expressed?' Medium comparison frame required.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a strong counter-argument paragraph
atomic_skills.description: Construct a counter-argument paragraph at quality 4 with a concession signal, a fair representation of the opposing view, a rebuttal connector, at least 2 supporting reasons, and evidence for at least 1 reason.

error_signatures.description: Opposing view extreme or absurd (meaning similarity below 0.30)
error_signatures.example: Opposing side caricatured rather than represented

error_signatures.description: Rebuttal with at most 1 supporting reason
error_signatures.example: Rebuttal asserts disagreement with one weak reason

error_signatures.description: Two reasons stated but no evidence
error_signatures.example: Rebuttal reasons given with no cited support

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: STRAW_MAN: 'State the strongest version of the opposing view — what would its best supporter say?' REBUTTAL_UNSUPPORTED: 2 reasons why the opposing view fails — use: 'This ignores / This overlooks / Research shows...'

atomic_skills.title: Using precise academic vocabulary
atomic_skills.description: Deploy nuanced academic vocabulary with a vocabulary variety score of at least 15% of total tokens, zero vague intensifiers without evidence, and at least 3 discipline-specific terms per literary essay.

error_signatures.description: Academic proportion below 10% across 2 consecutive tasks
error_signatures.example: Essay uses few academic-list words

error_signatures.description: More than 2 empty intensifiers
error_signatures.example: 'very', 'really' used without evidence repeatedly

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 discipline-specific terms per literary essay
error_signatures.example: No use of motif, diction, or juxtaposition

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: AWL_LOW: academic vocabulary expansion drill — 10 AWL words per task with contextual use tasks. DISCIPLINE_TERM_LOW: literary term list; at least 3 must be checked off per essay before submission.

atomic_skills.title: Sustaining an 800-word essay in one session
atomic_skills.description: Sustain an 800-word essay (single session) by meeting the 750-900 word target checked at submission, maintaining full structure, and avoiding quality degradation in the final body paragraph (coherence maintenance ratio >=0.85).

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 600 words at submission
error_signatures.example: Essay submitted at 540 words

error_signatures.description: Final body paragraph coherence significantly lower (ratio below 0.75)
error_signatures.example: Last paragraph is markedly weaker than the first

error_signatures.description: Missing conclusion or counter-argument
error_signatures.example: Essay ends with no conclusion

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: UNDER_LENGTH_TIMED: content audit — identify which section is underweight; targeted expansion drills. QUALITY_DEGRADATION: 'Your last paragraph is weaker than your first — write your strongest paragraph last.'

atomic_skills.title: Spotting whose viewpoint is being centred
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate ideological positioning in text by identifying the dominant ideology, naming the group whose perspective is centred or marginalised, linking to at least 2 specific language choices, and stating the effect on reader positioning.

error_signatures.description: Ideological reading without a predefined label
error_signatures.example: Learner describes a worldview without naming it

error_signatures.description: Centred perspective named, marginalised not identified
error_signatures.example: Only the dominant group is named

error_signatures.description: Ideology identified but reader effect not stated
error_signatures.example: Ideology named with no effect on the reader

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: IDEOLOGY_UNLABELLED: ideology predefined list; label required before analysis proceeds. READER_POSITIONING_ABSENT: 'How does this ideological choice position the reader — to agree, question, or resist?'

atomic_skills.title: Spotting manipulation techniques in media
atomic_skills.description: Identify manipulation in media texts by naming at least 3 manipulation techniques, each with a stated mechanism describing how the audience's psychology is guided and a stated effect.

error_signatures.description: Manipulation described without a predefined list name
error_signatures.example: Learner describes the trick without naming false urgency

error_signatures.description: Technique and effect given but no mechanism explanation
error_signatures.example: Effect stated with no 'it works by ___'

error_signatures.description: 'it convinces' without a specific belief, feeling, or action
error_signatures.example: No stated belief the audience is led toward

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TECHNIQUE_UNLABELLED: manipulation predefined list; label required before analysis proceeds. MECHANISM_ABSENT: 'How does it work on the audience? What psychological process does it use?'

atomic_skills.title: Writing a balanced, evaluated argument
atomic_skills.description: Produce a balanced evaluative argument with at least 2 arguments per position, an evaluative judgement based on stated criteria, and a conclusion that acknowledges complexity without false equivalence.

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 arguments per position
error_signatures.example: Only the favoured side is argued

error_signatures.description: Judgement without named evaluative criteria
error_signatures.example: Conclusion picks a side with no criteria

error_signatures.description: 'both sides are equally valid' without differentiation
error_signatures.example: Conclusion treats positions as identical in strength

error_signatures.description: Conclusion avoids stating the stronger position
error_signatures.example: Essay ends without committing

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CRITERIA_ABSENT: criteria card; minimum 2 must be invoked before conclusion. FALSE_EQUIVALENCE: 'On balance, which argument has stronger evidence? State this clearly.'

atomic_skills.title: Comparing two unseen texts
atomic_skills.description: Compare two unseen texts on a related topic by identifying at least 2 similarities and 2 differences in purpose, audience, tone, or approach, with a textual reference per point and an overall comparative judgement.

error_signatures.description: Similarity or difference stated without comparison language
error_signatures.example: A difference given with no 'whereas' or 'however'

error_signatures.description: Comparison point made with no textual support
error_signatures.example: A similarity asserted with no quote

error_signatures.description: Comparison completed without an overall effectiveness evaluation
error_signatures.example: No statement of which text is more effective

error_signatures.description: Only one text referenced across the comparison
error_signatures.example: Comparison discusses only Text A

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COMPARISON_CONNECTOR_ABSENT: comparison connector list required; each point must use a listed connector before submission. JUDGEMENT_ABSENT: 'Which text achieves its purpose more effectively, and why?' Evaluative sentence required before submission accepted.

atomic_skills.title: Identifying an author's bias and perspective
atomic_skills.description: Identify and explain an author's bias and perspective in an unseen text by naming the bias type, identifying at least 2 specific language choices revealing bias, explaining each choice's effect on reader positioning, and assessing the bias's impact on credibility.

error_signatures.description: Bias described but not named from taxonomy
error_signatures.example: One-sidedness noted without naming framing_bias

error_signatures.description: Bias identified at text level with no specific word or phrase cited
error_signatures.example: Bias asserted with no loaded word quoted

error_signatures.description: Reader effect stated without a positioning verb
error_signatures.example: 'It is biased' with no 'positions the reader'

error_signatures.description: Bias analysis completed without overall credibility judgement
error_signatures.example: No statement on whether bias weakens the text

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: BIAS_UNLABELLED_L13: predefined bias taxonomy with defining features; learner matches description to label before free analysis. CREDIBILITY_ABSENT: 'Does this bias make the argument more or less convincing? State your view and give one reason.' Required before submission.

atomic_skills.title: Synthesising two unseen texts to support a position
atomic_skills.description: Synthesise information from two unseen texts to support a stated analytical position, using at least one piece of evidence from each, integrating evidence smoothly, and demonstrating a coherent line of reasoning connecting evidence to the position.

error_signatures.description: Only one text referenced in the synthesis
error_signatures.example: Synthesis draws on Text A only

error_signatures.description: Evidence placed as a standalone sentence without integration
error_signatures.example: A quotation sits on its own line

error_signatures.description: Evidence cited without connecting reasoning to the stated position
error_signatures.example: Two quotes given with no analysis

error_signatures.description: Topic sentence disconnected from evidence (meaning connection below 0.30)
error_signatures.example: Topic sentence unrelated to the cited evidence

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SINGLE_SOURCE_ONLY_L13: 'Your synthesis must draw on both texts. Identify one piece of evidence from each before writing.' Evidence-first frame required. QUOTE_DUMP_L13: evidence integration drill — quote must appear inside the learner's own clause; three embedded examples required before free synthesis.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a formal report
atomic_skills.description: Write a formal report on a given issue with a clear heading and purpose statement, an introduction, at least 2 findings sections with subheadings, and a recommendations section, in fully objective register (250-350 words).

error_signatures.description: Heading, findings, or recommendations section missing
error_signatures.example: Report has no recommendations section

error_signatures.description: First-person opinion marker detected in a formal report
error_signatures.example: 'I think the data shows' in the findings

error_signatures.description: Findings described without an objective reporting verb
error_signatures.example: Findings narrated casually with no 'indicates'

error_signatures.description: No modal recommendation verb in the recommendations section
error_signatures.example: Recommendations stated with no 'should' or 'must'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: STRUCTURE_INCOMPLETE_REPORT: report template displayed with all section labels; each section must be completed before submission. REGISTER_SUBJECTIVE_REPORT: flagged tokens highlighted; replaced with objective equivalents before resubmission.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a review with clear criteria
atomic_skills.description: Write a review of a product, event, or text introducing the subject, applying at least 3 evaluative criteria with evidence per criterion, providing a balanced judgement, and including a recommendation (220-300 words).

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 evaluative criteria applied
error_signatures.example: Review judges on quality only

error_signatures.description: Criterion stated without supporting evidence or example
error_signatures.example: 'The plot was weak' with no example

error_signatures.description: Only positive or only negative evaluation, no balance
error_signatures.example: Review praises everything

error_signatures.description: No clear recommendation with a reason
error_signatures.example: Review ends with no 'would recommend'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ONE_SIDED_REVIEW: 'Your review must include both strengths and weaknesses. Add at least one point from the opposite side.' Balance check required before submission. CRITERIA_COUNT_LOW_REVIEW: criteria frame — 3 rows (criterion / evidence / judgement); all 3 rows must be completed before free writing.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a dialogue between two positions
atomic_skills.description: Write a dialogue between two speakers representing different positions where each states a position, gives at least 1 reason, responds directly to the other speaker, and maintains consistent register over at least 6 exchanges (200-280 words).

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 6 speaker exchanges
error_signatures.example: Dialogue has only 4 turns

error_signatures.description: Speaker states a position without any supporting reason
error_signatures.example: A speaker asserts a view with no 'because'

error_signatures.description: Speaker turn has no reference to the preceding speaker's point
error_signatures.example: Speakers state views without engaging each other

error_signatures.description: Speaker register shifts unexpectedly mid-dialogue
error_signatures.example: A formal speaker suddenly uses slang

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TALKING_PAST: 'Each response must acknowledge what the other speaker just said.' Response template: 'You said [reference] — however, [counter].' Required before free writing. TURN_COUNT_LOW: minimum 6 turns enforced; system does not accept submission until turn count is at least 6.

atomic_skills.title: Rewriting sentences for clarity
atomic_skills.description: Rewrite 6 sentences containing redundancy, weak verbs, or unclear structure to remove the identified problem while preserving meaning, stating the specific improvement made for each.

error_signatures.description: Rewritten sentence meaning similarity to original below 0.45
error_signatures.example: Rewrite changes the original idea

error_signatures.description: Identified problem persists in the rewrite
error_signatures.example: Redundant phrase still present after rewrite

error_signatures.description: Sentence rewritten but improvement type not stated
error_signatures.example: Rewrite given with no improvement label

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PROBLEM_REMAINS: sentence shown with problem highlighted; specific instruction given (e.g., 'Remove the underlined redundant phrase'). Targeted drill before free rewrite. MEANING_LOST_REWRITE: 'Your rewrite has changed the meaning. Compare your sentence with the original. Revise to restore the original idea.'

atomic_skills.title: Replacing vague vocabulary with precise words
atomic_skills.description: Identify at least 4 instances of vague, overused, or imprecise vocabulary in a provided text, replace each with a precise alternative, and explain why the replacement is more precise.

error_signatures.description: Vague token from the predefined list not identified
error_signatures.example: Learner overlooks 'thing' in the text

error_signatures.description: Replacement word also on the imprecision list or meaning connection below 0.35
error_signatures.example: 'good' replaced with 'nice'

error_signatures.description: Replacement made but precision reason not stated
