error_signatures.example: Word swapped with no explanation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: IMPRECISION_MISSED: predefined imprecision token list displayed; learner scans text against the list before free identification. REPLACEMENT_IMPRECISE: 'Your replacement is still vague. Try a word that specifies exactly how much, how, or what kind.' Replacement reattempted.

atomic_skills.title: Editing a paragraph for register, grammar and flow
atomic_skills.description: Edit a full paragraph for register consistency, grammar accuracy, and cohesion by identifying and correcting all register inconsistencies, grammatical errors, and missing or misused cohesion devices, producing a clean edited version with changes justified.

error_signatures.description: Informal tokens remain after editing
error_signatures.example: Contractions survive the edit

error_signatures.description: Grammatical error not identified or correction wrong
error_signatures.example: An SVA error persists after editing

error_signatures.description: Missing or broken connector not fixed
error_signatures.example: A logical jump left without a transition

error_signatures.description: Edit made but taxonomy label not applied
error_signatures.example: Change made with no register_fix or grammar_fix label

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REGISTER_REMAINING: flagged tokens shown after edit; each must be corrected before resubmission. GRAMMAR_ERROR_REMAINING: specific error type shown with rule card; targeted correction required before proceeding.

atomic_skills.title: Giving an extended oral argument
atomic_skills.description: Deliver an extended oral argument stating a clear position, providing at least 3 supported arguments, including at least 1 counter-argument with rebuttal, and concluding with a synthesis statement in formal register (250-350 words).

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 supported arguments
error_signatures.example: Speaker makes only two supported points

error_signatures.description: No concession plus rebuttal structure
error_signatures.example: Argument ignores the opposing view

error_signatures.description: Conclusion restates position without added depth
error_signatures.example: Conclusion is a flat repeat of the opening

error_signatures.description: Informal markers in an extended argument
error_signatures.example: Slang used in the spoken argument

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COUNTERARG_ABSENT_ORAL: concession plus rebuttal frame — 'It may be argued that [opposition]. However, [rebuttal] because [reason].' Must be inserted before submission. SYNTHESIS_ABSENT_ORAL: 'Your conclusion must go beyond restating your position. What does your argument reveal?' Qualifier or broadening clause required.

atomic_skills.title: Answering panel-interview questions
atomic_skills.description: Respond to a simulated panel interview by answering 4 questions precisely within 50-80 words each, maintaining formal register, demonstrating reasoning beyond factual recall, and concluding each response with a specific point.

error_signatures.description: Answer meaning connection to question below 0.35
error_signatures.example: Answer addresses a different question

error_signatures.description: Answer contains factual restatement only, no reasoning connector
error_signatures.example: Answer recites a fact with no 'because'

error_signatures.description: Answer under 40 or over 100 words
error_signatures.example: Answer is a single short clause

error_signatures.description: Answer ends with a filler phrase
error_signatures.example: Answer ends with 'thank you, that is all'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REASONING_ABSENT_INTERVIEW: 'Add a reason for your answer. Use: because / this means / as a result.' Sentence extender required. FILLER_CONCLUSION: 'End with a specific point, not a closing phrase.' Example of a specific concluding claim displayed.

atomic_skills.title: Evaluating a speech transcript
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate a transcript of a speech or debate by identifying at least 2 strengths and 2 weaknesses of the speaker's argument, naming at least 1 rhetorical technique, rating the persuasive effectiveness, and justifying the rating with at least 2 reasons.

error_signatures.description: Only strengths or only weaknesses identified
error_signatures.example: Evaluation lists strengths but no weaknesses

error_signatures.description: Strength or weakness stated without a transcript reference
error_signatures.example: 'The argument was weak' with no quote

error_signatures.description: Rhetorical technique described but not named from the list
error_signatures.example: Repetition noted without naming anaphora

error_signatures.description: Overall rating stated with fewer than 2 reasons
error_signatures.example: 'Moderately persuasive' with no reasons

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: EVALUATION_ONE_SIDED_SPEECH: 'Your evaluation must include both strengths and weaknesses.' Balance check enforced before submission. RATING_UNJUSTIFIED: 'State your rating and give two reasons for it.' Rating plus reasons frame required.

levels.title: NSC Exit Standard
levels.description: Perform at NSC exam standard — unseen poetry analysis, 700-900 word essays, intellectual maturity, and full TICC integration with distinction-level evaluation of ambiguity and layered argument. Grade 12, mixed reading + writing + voice. Assessment is single-session, with word count checked at submission (no real-time pacing). Advance when thesis originality is HIGH, TICC is present per paragraph, command precision >=60%, coherence >=60%, grammar GREEN or AMBER, 700-900 words, across 3 non-consecutive sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Analysing unseen poetry
atomic_skills.description: Analyse unseen poetry by integrating all 4 TICC dimensions in a single analytical paragraph, naming at least 4 devices with effect plus structural analysis, and producing an original interpretive claim not present in the prompt.

error_signatures.description: At least 1 TICC dimension absent
error_signatures.example: Analysis covers Theme and Craft but omits Context

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 4 devices per poem
error_signatures.example: Only two devices named

error_signatures.description: No form feature analysed
error_signatures.example: No comment on stanza form or line length

error_signatures.description: Original claim meaning similarity to prompt at or above 0.50
error_signatures.example: Interpretive claim restates the question

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TICC_INCOMPLETE: TICC checklist gate; each dimension must be completed before submission accepted. PARAPHRASED_CLAIM: 'Your interpretive claim must go beyond what the question states — what original insight do you bring?'

atomic_skills.title: Reading exam command words precisely
atomic_skills.description: Respond precisely to command words so analyse, evaluate, discuss, and compare produce detectably different response types in analytical verb density, judgement, balance, and comparison language.

error_signatures.description: Evaluate responded to as analyse (judgement absent)
error_signatures.example: An 'evaluate' task answered with decomposition only

error_signatures.description: Discuss task with a balance failure
error_signatures.example: A 'discuss' task argues only one side

error_signatures.description: Comparison without both texts referenced per statement
error_signatures.example: A 'compare' task discusses only Text A

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COMMAND_CONFUSION: command word predefined list — 'Evaluate = judge using criteria; Analyse = break down without judging.' Differentiation task: same passage, 4 command word responses, each detectably different. DISCUSS_ONE_SIDED: balance check — both sides must be represented.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a layered literary essay (theme, intent, context, craft)
atomic_skills.description: Construct 3-4 body paragraph literary essays where each paragraph integrates all TICC dimensions, with quote integration at least 95%, analytical coherence, thesis link, no scaffold dependency, and coherence maintained from first to final paragraph.

error_signatures.description: TICC dimensions fewer than 4 per paragraph
error_signatures.example: A paragraph integrates only Theme and Intention

error_signatures.description: Quote not embedded in the learner's clause
error_signatures.example: Quotation placed on its own line

error_signatures.description: Coherence ratio drops significantly across the essay
error_signatures.example: Final paragraph much weaker than the first

error_signatures.description: Final sentence does not connect to the thesis
error_signatures.example: Paragraph ends with no tie back to the thesis

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TICC_INCOMPLETE: TICC checklist gate (same as L14.A1); each dimension must be identifiable before submission accepted. COHERENCE_DEGRADATION: 'Your last paragraph is weaker than your first — reverse your order; draft conclusion first.'

atomic_skills.title: Writing a full 700–900 word essay in one session
atomic_skills.description: Write 700-900 word essays in a single session with full structure (introduction plus 3-4 body plus conclusion), editing evidence before submission, and a coherence maintenance ratio of at least 0.90. Word count is checked at submission, no real-time pacing.

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 600 words at submission
error_signatures.example: Essay submitted at 540 words

error_signatures.description: More than 1000 words (focus concern)
error_signatures.example: Essay runs to 1100 words

error_signatures.description: Coherence maintenance ratio below 0.80 (quality drops across the essay)
error_signatures.example: Argument quality collapses by the final paragraph

error_signatures.description: No revision evidence before submission
error_signatures.example: Essay submitted with no editing pass

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: UNDER_LENGTH_TIMED: content diagnostics; identify the underweight section; targeted expansion drills. COHERENCE_DEGRADATION: reverse drafting — conclusion written first to anchor quality.

atomic_skills.title: Bringing theme, intent, context and craft into one essay
atomic_skills.description: Integrate all four TICC dimensions in analytical writing so that Theme, Intention, Context, and Craft are all identifiable and mutually reinforcing within a paragraph or analysis section.

error_signatures.description: Any TICC dimension absent
error_signatures.example: Context dimension missing from the paragraph

error_signatures.description: All 4 present but no inter-dimension connection detected
error_signatures.example: Dimensions listed separately with no links

error_signatures.description: Craft is only a technique name, no structural feature
error_signatures.example: 'Uses metaphor' with no structural analysis

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TICC_INCOMPLETE: TICC checklist gate (same as L14.A1). TICC_DISCONNECTED: 'How does the craft choice connect to the authorial intention? How does the context shape the theme?' Cross-dimension linking prompt.

atomic_skills.title: Evaluating what the author was trying to do
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate authorial intention by stating the author's purpose, naming at least 2 craft choices that serve that intention, and evaluating how successfully the text achieves it with at least 2 criteria.

error_signatures.description: 'to entertain' or 'to inform' without a specific proposition
error_signatures.example: Purpose given as 'to inform' with no detail

error_signatures.description: Craft choices stated without connection to the stated purpose
error_signatures.example: Devices listed with no tie to intention

error_signatures.description: Effectiveness stated without named criteria
error_signatures.example: 'It succeeds' with no criteria

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PURPOSE_VAGUE: 'What specific belief or feeling does this author want the reader to have?' Specific proposition required. JUDGEMENT_WITHOUT_CRITERIA: evaluation criteria card; minimum 2 must be invoked.

atomic_skills.title: Showing more than one valid reading of a text
atomic_skills.description: Demonstrate nuanced interpretation by producing at least 2 plausible but distinct interpretations of the same textual element, the evidence for each, and an analysis of why the text supports both readings with neither dismissed.

error_signatures.description: Only one interpretation offered
error_signatures.example: Learner gives a single reading of an ambiguous line

error_signatures.description: One reading acknowledged then discarded without analysis
error_signatures.example: Second reading mentioned then waved away

error_signatures.description: Dual reading claimed without naming what allows it
error_signatures.example: Two readings given with no irony or symbol named

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SINGLE_READING: 'This text can be read in more than one way. What else might it mean?' Second reading prompt required. AMBIGUITY_FEATURE_ABSENT: 'A nuanced reader holds both readings simultaneously — what textual feature allows this?'

atomic_skills.title: Writing an original thesis (not a paraphrase)
atomic_skills.description: Construct an original thesis that is not a paraphrase of the question, makes a claimable critical position, and introduces an interpretive angle not obvious from a surface reading.

error_signatures.description: Similarity to the question at or above 0.45
error_signatures.example: Thesis restates the essay question

error_signatures.description: Similarity to a surface reading at or above 0.40
error_signatures.example: Thesis states the obvious plot point

error_signatures.description: Abstract claim with no specific textual grounding
error_signatures.example: A vague universal statement with no anchor

error_signatures.description: No critical position (not claimable)
error_signatures.example: Thesis describes rather than argues

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: THESIS_PARAPHRASE: 'Your thesis restates the question — what is your own interpretive claim?' Distance drill: rewrite until similarity below 0.45. THESIS_OBVIOUS: 'What is surprising or counterintuitive about this text? Build your thesis from there.'

atomic_skills.title: Reading ambiguity as a feature, not a flaw
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate ambiguity in texts by identifying at least 2 genuinely indeterminate elements, naming the textual or linguistic feature creating each, and stating the interpretive implications of each reading without resolving to a single meaning.

error_signatures.description: Dual reading identified then resolved to a single meaning
error_signatures.example: Two readings collapsed into one conclusion

error_signatures.description: Ambiguity named without a predefined label
error_signatures.example: Ambiguity noted without naming tonal irony

error_signatures.description: Only 1 ambiguous element identified
error_signatures.example: Only one indeterminate element discussed

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: AMBIGUITY_RESOLVED: 'A sophisticated reader sits with uncertainty. What if both interpretations are equally valid?' Resolution-resistance frame: 'The text permits both... and... simultaneously because...' AMBIGUITY_TYPE_ABSENT: ambiguity predefined list.

atomic_skills.title: Holding two positions in tension in one essay
atomic_skills.description: Construct a layered argument that argues at least 2 simultaneous positions held in productive tension, connects layers through a unifying interpretive insight, and sustains complexity to the conclusion.

error_signatures.description: Argument layers collapse to a simple for/against
error_signatures.example: Two positions reduced to a single binary

error_signatures.description: Both positions stated but no 'and yet' framing
error_signatures.example: Positions presented sequentially, not simultaneously

error_signatures.description: Layers unconnected in the conclusion
error_signatures.example: Conclusion does not connect the two positions

error_signatures.description: Argument simplified to a single position before the conclusion
error_signatures.example: Tension dropped halfway through the essay

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: FLAT_ARGUMENT: 'Instead of arguing for or against, the text reveals a tension between two ideas that both matter.' UNIFYING_INSIGHT_ABSENT: 'How do your two positions connect at a deeper level? What does their coexistence reveal?'

atomic_skills.title: Writing a stylistically sophisticated essay
atomic_skills.description: Write a stylistically sophisticated essay with sentence variety, at least 2 distinct rhetorical techniques, AWL at least 18%, at least 3 discipline-specific terms, an empty-intensifier rate of zero, and readable academic sophistication.

error_signatures.description: No rhetorical technique detected
error_signatures.example: No anaphora, tricolon, chiasmus, or parenthetical

error_signatures.description: AWL below 15% across 2 consecutive tasks
error_signatures.example: Essay uses few academic-list words

error_signatures.description: Any empty intensifier without a specific claim or evidence
error_signatures.example: 'very important' with no support

error_signatures.description: Consecutive same-structure openings
error_signatures.example: Three sentences in a row open identically

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TECHNIQUE_ABSENT: rhetorical technique list; at least 2 must be marked in text before submission. INTENSIFIER_PRESENT: submission rejected for intensifier; replace with specific evidence or claim.

atomic_skills.title: Comparing multiple critical readings of one text
atomic_skills.description: Analyse multiple interpretations of the same text by presenting at least 3 interpretive positions from different critical frameworks, evaluating the explanatory power of each with a textual example, and stating which is most compelling with at least 2 reasons.

error_signatures.description: Interpretation without a critical framework label
error_signatures.example: A reading given with no feminist or Marxist label

error_signatures.description: Framework claimed without textual evidence
error_signatures.example: A framework named with no textual example

error_signatures.description: Frameworks compared but no preference stated
error_signatures.example: No statement of which framework is most compelling

error_signatures.description: Frameworks listed separately without comparative evaluation
error_signatures.example: Three readings given side by side with no comparison

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: FRAMEWORK_ABSENT: critical framework predefined list with defining questions per framework. COMPARISON_ABSENT: 'Which framework explains most about this text? Which has the greatest explanatory power?'

atomic_skills.title: Producing exam-ready writing consistently
atomic_skills.description: Produce exam-ready responses consistently across all P1/P2/P3 task types with command word precision, word count targets met, complete structure, scaffold dependency below 3%, and a coherence maintenance ratio of at least 0.90.

error_signatures.description: Below 85% command precision
error_signatures.example: Frequent command-word mismatches across tasks

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 90% of submissions in the target word range
error_signatures.example: Several essays under or over the target length

error_signatures.description: More than 10% of tasks with incomplete structure
error_signatures.example: Multiple essays missing a conclusion

error_signatures.description: Frame patterns above 3%
error_signatures.example: Provided sentence frames still appear in submissions

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COMMAND_PRECISION_LOW: command differentiation task battery. WORD_COUNT_FAILURE: targeted drill for the specific section where count consistently drops.

atomic_skills.title: Reading subtext and irony
atomic_skills.description: Interpret implicit meaning, subtext, and irony by identifying at least 2 instances per text, explaining what is implied versus stated, naming the feature creating the gap, and connecting each instance to the author's broader purpose.

error_signatures.description: Implied meaning phrase found directly in the source text
error_signatures.example: Learner cites an explicit sentence as subtext

error_signatures.description: Subtext or irony identified but creating feature not named
error_signatures.example: Irony noted without naming understatement

error_signatures.description: Implied meaning stated without articulating stated versus intended
error_signatures.example: Only the implied side explained, not the contrast

error_signatures.description: Subtext identified but not connected to broader authorial purpose
error_signatures.example: Irony explained with no link to the author's aim

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: STATED_AS_IMPLICIT_L14: 'Your interpretation is already in the text. Find what the author hints at without saying.' Keyword check before resubmission. GAP_UNEXPLAINED: frame — 'The text says [stated]. What the author actually means is [implied]. This gap is created by [feature].' Required before acceptance.

atomic_skills.title: Evaluating an author's structural and language choices
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of an author's structural and language choices by identifying at least 2 structural and 2 language choices, explaining each effect on meaning or reader response, and producing an overall effectiveness judgement with at least 2 criterion-based reasons.

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 structural or fewer than 2 language choices
error_signatures.example: Only one structural choice identified

error_signatures.description: Choice identified but effect described without a purpose-achievement verb
error_signatures.example: 'It is effective' with no 'reinforces' or 'positions'

error_signatures.description: Only one category of choice identified
error_signatures.example: Only language choices given, no structural ones

error_signatures.description: Effectiveness stated with no criterion-based reasoning
error_signatures.example: 'Highly effective' with no criteria

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: EFFECT_VAGUE_L14: 'State specifically what this choice achieves — how does it affect the reader or advance the author's purpose?' Purpose-achievement verb required before acceptance. JUDGEMENT_WITHOUT_CRITERIA_L14: 'Your judgement must be supported by at least two criteria. Name them and explain.' Criteria frame required.

atomic_skills.title: Synthesising three or more sources into one position
atomic_skills.description: Synthesise perspectives from three or more sources into a coherent analytical position by integrating evidence from each, demonstrating agreement and tension between sources, and constructing an original position that goes beyond any single source (300-400 words).

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 sources referenced
error_signatures.example: Synthesis draws on only two sources

error_signatures.description: Evidence placed as a standalone sentence in synthesis
error_signatures.example: A quotation sits on its own line

error_signatures.description: Sources cited sequentially with no comparison between them
error_signatures.example: Sources summarised one after another with no relation

error_signatures.description: Synthesised position meaning similarity to a single source at or above 0.55
error_signatures.example: Position simply restates one source's view

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: INTER_SOURCE_TENSION_ABSENT: 'Do your sources agree or disagree? Identify one point of tension or agreement between them.' Comparative connector required before submission. POSITION_NOT_ORIGINAL_L14: 'Your position restates one source. What conclusion do you draw from all three sources together?' Originality check enforced.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a formal article at NSC exit standard
atomic_skills.description: Write a formal article for an academic or professional audience opening with a thesis-driven introduction, developing at least 3 substantiated sections with evidence and analysis, addressing a counter-perspective, and concluding with a synthesis insight in fully academic register (350-450 words).

error_signatures.description: Thesis is a topic label rather than a claimable position
error_signatures.example: Opening names a topic without arguing a position

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 substantiated sections
error_signatures.example: Article develops only two sections

error_signatures.description: No acknowledgement of an opposing view
error_signatures.example: Article presents one side only

error_signatures.description: Conclusion restates the introduction without added insight
error_signatures.example: Conclusion is a flat repeat of the opening

error_signatures.description: Informal markers or AWL below 10%
error_signatures.example: Casual phrasing in the article body

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: THESIS_VAGUE_ARTICLE: 'Your opening must argue a specific, debatable position — not describe a topic.' Thesis revision required before body writing. COUNTER_PERSPECTIVE_ABSENT: counter-perspective frame — concession signal + rebuttal + reason; must be inserted before submission.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a structured set of interview answers
atomic_skills.description: Write a structured interview response set answering 5 challenging questions with precise answers demonstrating evaluative thinking, formal register, discipline-specific vocabulary, and one answer demonstrating acknowledgement of complexity with appropriate hedging (60-90 words each).

error_signatures.description: Answer contains only factual restatement, no evaluative verb
error_signatures.example: An answer recites facts with no judgement

error_signatures.description: No hedging marker in any answer where complexity is evident
error_signatures.example: A complex answer states everything as certain

error_signatures.description: Informal markers or AWL below 12%
error_signatures.example: Casual phrasing in an interview answer

error_signatures.description: Answer under 50 or over 110 words
error_signatures.example: An answer is a single short sentence

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: RECALL_ONLY_L14: 'Add a judgement — what do you conclude about this? Use: I argue/this demonstrates/this challenges.' Evaluative verb required. HEDGING_ABSENT_L14: 'Acknowledge what is uncertain or complex. Use: it could be argued/arguably/it is possible that.' Hedging sentence required in the relevant answer.

atomic_skills.title: Writing a distinction-level persuasive speech
atomic_skills.description: Write a persuasive speech at distinction level opening with a rhetorical device, developing a layered argument, deploying at least 2 distinct rhetorical techniques, maintaining formal register, and closing with a call to action or unifying insight (350-450 words).

error_signatures.description: No detectable rhetorical device in the opening
error_signatures.example: Speech opens with a plain statement

error_signatures.description: Single-layer position only, no supporting layer or resolution
error_signatures.example: Speech makes one claim with no second layer

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 distinct rhetorical techniques
error_signatures.example: Only one technique used across the speech

error_signatures.description: Informal markers or AWL below 12%
error_signatures.example: Casual phrasing in the speech

error_signatures.description: Speech ends with a summary restatement rather than a call to action or unifying insight
error_signatures.example: Speech closes by repeating the opening

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ARGUMENT_FLAT_SPEECH: 'Your argument must have more than one layer. Add a supporting claim and a resolution that connects your positions.' Layered argument frame required. TECHNIQUE_COUNT_LOW_SPEECH: rhetorical technique list; two distinct techniques must be inserted and marked before submission.

atomic_skills.title: Doing a full language audit of your own essay
atomic_skills.description: Perform a full language audit of own essay at NSC exit standard reviewing grammar accuracy, register consistency, punctuation precision, word choice precision, and AWL proportion, reporting findings by category and correcting all identified errors.

error_signatures.description: Grammar errors remaining after audit above 10%
error_signatures.example: An SVA error survives the audit

error_signatures.description: Informal tokens present after the audit
error_signatures.example: A contraction remains after editing

error_signatures.description: Empty intensifiers present in the edited essay
error_signatures.example: 'very' remains without support

error_signatures.description: AWL proportion in edited text below 12%
error_signatures.example: Edited essay still has low academic vocabulary

error_signatures.description: Punctuation errors remaining after audit above 10%
error_signatures.example: A comma splice survives the audit

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REGISTER_REMAINING_L14: all informal tokens highlighted; each must be replaced with a formal equivalent before the audit is accepted. AWL_LOW_AUDIT: 'Your academic vocabulary proportion is below target. Identify 3 words that could be replaced with AWL alternatives.' Replacement task required.

atomic_skills.title: Improving sentence complexity in a draft
atomic_skills.description: Improve sentence complexity at distinction level by rewriting 6 simple or compound sentences as compound-complex or complex sentences without losing meaning, demonstrating at least 2 different subordination strategies, and explaining the structural improvement per sentence.

error_signatures.description: Rewritten sentence contains no dependent clause
error_signatures.example: Rewrite remains a simple sentence

error_signatures.description: Rewritten sentence meaning similarity to original below 0.50
error_signatures.example: Rewrite changes the original idea

error_signatures.description: All rewrites use the same subordination strategy
error_signatures.example: Every rewrite uses a relative clause

error_signatures.description: Rewrite passes but structural improvement type not stated
error_signatures.example: Rewrite given with no improvement label

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: STILL_SIMPLE_L14: subordination strategy list with examples; learner selects and applies one strategy before free rewrite. SUBORDINATION_TYPE_NARROW: 'Your rewrites use the same structure. Apply a different subordination strategy in at least two sentences.' Strategy variety check required.

atomic_skills.title: Replacing imprecise words with academic vocabulary
atomic_skills.description: Demonstrate vocabulary precision at distinction level by replacing at least 5 imprecise or overused words in a low-register text with AWL or discipline-appropriate alternatives, justifying each by the semantic gain, and ensuring the edited text reaches AWL proportion at least 18%.

error_signatures.description: Replacement word not on AWL and specificity increase below 0.20
error_signatures.example: 'good' replaced with another vague word

error_signatures.description: Edited text AWL proportion below 15%
error_signatures.example: Edited text still has low academic vocabulary

error_signatures.description: Justification states 'better' or 'more academic' without a specific semantic gain descriptor
error_signatures.example: 'It sounds better' with no descriptor

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 5 replacements made
error_signatures.example: Only 3 words replaced

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REPLACEMENT_NOT_AWL: AWL list displayed; learner selects a replacement from the list and checks it fits the context. JUSTIFICATION_SURFACE_L14: semantic gain descriptor list displayed (specificity/register elevation/connotative precision/denotative accuracy); descriptor must be selected and applied before acceptance.

atomic_skills.title: Giving a formal NSC-standard speech on an unseen topic
atomic_skills.description: Produce a prepared formal speech at NSC standard on an unseen topic constructing a layered argument, deploying at least 2 rhetorical techniques, maintaining academic register, citing at least 1 named source or statistic, and closing with a unifying insight (350-450 words).

error_signatures.description: Single-layer argument, no tension or supporting layer
error_signatures.example: Speech makes one claim with no second layer

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 2 rhetorical techniques
error_signatures.example: Only one technique used in the speech

error_signatures.description: No named source or statistic cited
error_signatures.example: Speech cites no evidence

error_signatures.description: Conclusion paraphrases the opening rather than elevating the argument
error_signatures.example: Conclusion repeats the opening point

error_signatures.description: Informal markers or AWL below 12%
error_signatures.example: Casual phrasing in the speech

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ARGUMENT_FLAT_ORAL_L14: 'Your argument needs a second layer. What complexity or tension does your position acknowledge? Resolve it in the conclusion.' Layered argument frame required. CLOSING_INSIGHT_ABSENT: 'Your closing must reveal something larger than what your argument has already stated.' Superordinate claim frame: 'Ultimately, this reveals [broader insight].'

atomic_skills.title: Answering an unseen NSC oral exam set
atomic_skills.description: Respond to an unseen question set in a simulated NSC oral examination by answering 4 questions demonstrating command word precision, formal register, and reasoning beyond factual recall (70-100 words each).

error_signatures.description: Response type does not match command word requirements
error_signatures.example: An 'evaluate' question answered as 'analyse'

error_signatures.description: Answer contains no evaluative or synthesis verb
error_signatures.example: Answer recites facts with no judgement

error_signatures.description: Informal markers detected
error_signatures.example: Slang used in the spoken answer

error_signatures.description: Answer under 60 or over 120 words
error_signatures.example: Answer is a single short clause

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COMMAND_PRECISION_LOW_ORAL: command word differentiation card — analyse/evaluate/discuss/compare with defining response characteristics; learner identifies which type is required before answering. RECALL_ONLY_ORAL_L14: 'Your answer describes rather than evaluates. Add a judgement using: argues/concludes/challenges/demonstrates.' Evaluative verb required.

atomic_skills.title: Evaluating your own spoken argument transcript
atomic_skills.description: Critically evaluate own spoken argument transcript at distinction level by identifying at least 2 register lapses, 2 structural gaps, and 2 reasoning failures, proposing a specific revision for each, and producing an overall self-assessment with at least 3 criterion-based reasons.

error_signatures.description: Only surface features identified, no structural or reasoning issues
error_signatures.example: Self-evaluation lists only word-choice fixes

error_signatures.description: Proposed revision meaning similarity to original at or above 0.80
error_signatures.example: Revision barely changes the original wording

error_signatures.description: Gap identified without a predefined argument stage label
error_signatures.example: A gap noted without naming counter-argument

error_signatures.description: Reasoning issue identified without a predefined taxonomy label
error_signatures.example: A logical gap noted without naming it

error_signatures.description: Overall self-assessment rating stated with fewer than 3 reasons
error_signatures.example: A rating given with only one reason

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SELF_EVAL_SURFACE_L14: 'Your evaluation only addresses surface features. Now evaluate the structure and logic of your argument.' Structural and reasoning checklists displayed; each category requires at least 1 identified issue. REVISION_TOO_SIMILAR: 'Your proposed revision is too similar to the original. Revise substantially.' Revision similarity check enforced before acceptance.
